title.raw: 卷二百八十一 列傳第一百六十九 循吏 Volume 281 Biographies 169: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 【列傳第一百六十九循吏】

translations.literal: [Biography 169: Virtuous Officials]
translations.idiomatic: Biography 169: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 明太祖懲元季吏治縱弛，民生凋敝，重繩貪吏，置之嚴典。

translations.literal: The founding emperor of Ming, punishing the lax official governance at the end of Yuan and the withering of the people's livelihood, heavily constrained corrupt officials and placed them under strict statutes.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor, responding to the lax governance and devastated livelihoods of the late Yuan period, imposed heavy penalties on corrupt officials and subjected them to the strictest law.

sentences.zh: 府州縣吏來朝，陛辭，諭曰：「天下新定，百姓財力俱困，如鳥初飛，木初植，勿拔其羽，勿撼其根。

translations.literal: When prefectural, circuit, and county officials came to court and took leave at the throne, he instructed them, saying: "The realm has newly been settled; the people's wealth and strength are both exhausted, like a bird just beginning to fly or a tree just planted—do not pluck its feathers, do not shake its roots.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural and county officials came to court and took their leave at the throne, he instructed them: "The realm has only just been pacified. The people's resources are utterly depleted—as with a bird taking its first flight or a sapling newly planted, do not pluck its feathers or shake its roots.

sentences.zh: 然惟廉者能約己而愛人，貪者必朘人以肥己，爾等戒之。」

translations.literal: Yet only the incorruptible can restrain themselves and love others; the greedy must certainly extract from people to enrich themselves—you must guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Only the incorruptible can restrain themselves and care for the people; the greedy will inevitably bleed the people to fill their own pockets. Take warning.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年，下詔有司考課，首學校、農桑諸實政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu, an edict was issued for the responsible offices to conduct evaluations, putting first schools, agriculture, sericulture, and other substantive policies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongwu (1372), an edict ordered officials to conduct performance reviews, prioritizing schools, agriculture, sericulture, and other substantive achievements.

sentences.zh: 日照知縣馬亮善督運，無課農興士效，立命黜之。

translations.literal: Rizhao magistrate Ma Liang was skilled at supervising transport but had no effect in promoting agriculture or raising scholars; he was immediately ordered dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang, magistrate of Rizhao, was adept at supervising transport but showed no results in farming or education; he was promptly dismissed.

sentences.zh: 一時守令畏法，潔己愛民，以當上指，吏治煥然丕變矣。

translations.literal: For a time the prefects and magistrates feared the law, kept themselves pure and loved the people to meet the sovereign's intent, and official governance was brilliantly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: For a time prefects and magistrates feared the law, kept their conduct pure, and cared for the people to satisfy the emperor's wishes, and governance was utterly transformed.

sentences.zh: 下逮仁、宣，撫循休息，民人安樂，吏治澄清者百餘年。

translations.literal: Extending down through Renzong and Xuanzong, with comforting care and rest, the people were secure and happy, and official governance remained clear for more than a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Down through the reigns of Renzong and Xuanzong, with nourishing governance and policies of rest, the people lived in peace and contentment, and official administration remained clean for more than a century.

sentences.zh: 英、武之際，內外多故，而民心無土崩瓦解之虞者，亦由吏鮮貪殘，故禍亂易弭也。

translations.literal: During the reigns of Yingzong and Wuzong, though there were many troubles at home and abroad, yet the people's hearts had no fear of collapse and disintegration—this also was because officials rarely were greedy and cruel, so calamities and disorder were easily quelled.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Yingzong and Wuzong, despite many troubles at home and abroad, the people never faced the prospect of total collapse—largely because officials were seldom greedy or cruel, so disorder was easier to quell.

sentences.zh: 嘉、隆以後，資格既重甲科，縣令多以廉卓被征，梯取台省，而龔、黃之治，或未之覯焉。

translations.literal: After Jiajing and Longqing, since qualifications already valued the top examination degree, county magistrates were often summoned for incorruptibility and excellence and climbed to ministries and departments, yet the governance of Gong and Huang perhaps was no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiajing and Longqing reigns, as credentials increasingly favored top jinshi graduates, county magistrates were often promoted to the central ministries for reputations of probity and distinction, yet the exemplary governance of Gong Bin and Huang Zonghan was seldom seen again.

sentences.zh: 神宗末年，徵發頻仍，礦稅四出，海內騷然煩費，郡縣不克修舉厥職。

translations.literal: In the late years of Shenzong, levies and corvée were frequent, mining taxes issued in all directions, the realm was agitated and burdened with expenses, and the prefectures and counties could not fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Shenzong, levies and corvée came in rapid succession, mining taxes were imposed everywhere, the realm seethed with exactions and expense, and prefectures and counties could no longer perform their proper duties.

sentences.zh: 而廟堂考課，一切以虛文從事，不復加意循良之選。

translations.literal: Yet the court's evaluations were all conducted as empty formalities, and no further attention was given to selecting virtuous officials.
translations.idiomatic: Court evaluations became mere formalities, and no further care was given to selecting virtuous officials.

sentences.zh: 吏治既以日媮，民生由之益蹙。

translations.literal: Official governance daily deteriorated, and the people's livelihood thereby grew more strained.
translations.idiomatic: As governance daily declined, the people's livelihood grew ever more precarious.

sentences.zh: 仁、宣之盛，邈乎不可復追，而太祖之法蔑如矣。

translations.literal: The splendor of Renzong and Xuanzong was distant and could not be recovered, while the founding emperor's laws were treated with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The glory of the Ren-Xuan era was beyond recovery, and the Hongwu Emperor's laws were treated as nothing.

sentences.zh: 重內輕外，實政不修，謂非在上者不加之意使然乎！

translations.literal: Valuing the interior and slighting the exterior, substantive governance was not cultivated—can one say this was not caused by those above not giving it their attention!
translations.idiomatic: With attention fixed on the capital and neglect of the provinces, substantive governance withered—was this not because those at the top failed to attend to it?

sentences.zh: 漢史丞相黃霸，唐史節度使韋丹，皆入《循吏傳》中。

translations.literal: Han History's Chancellor Huang Ba and Tang History's military commissioner Wei Dan both entered the "Virtuous Officials" biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huang Ba of the Han History and Military Commissioner Wei Dan of the Tang History both appear in their respective Virtuous Officials chapters.

sentences.zh: 今自守令超擢至公卿有勳德者，事皆別見，故采其終於庶僚，政績可紀者，作《循吏傳》。

translations.literal: Now those promoted from magistrate to minister and ranking official with meritorious virtue have their affairs recorded elsewhere, so those who ended as common officials with recordable achievements are collected to compose the Virtuous Officials biography.
translations.idiomatic: Those magistrates promoted to high office with distinguished merit are treated in separate biographies; here we gather those who remained common officials yet left recordable achievements, composing this Virtuous Officials chapter.

sentences.zh: ○陳灌·方克勤·吳履·廖欽等·高鬥南·餘彥誠等·史誠祖·吳祥等·謝子襄·黃信中·夏升·貝秉彝·劉孟雍等·萬觀·葉宗人·王源·翟溥福·李信圭·孫浩等·張宗璉·李驥·王瑩等·李湘·趙豫·趙登等·曾泉·范衷·周濟·範希正·劉綱·段堅·陳鋼·丁積·田鐸·唐侃·湯紹恩·徐九思·龐嵩·張淳·陳幼學

sentences.zh: 陳灌，字子將，廬陵人也。

translations.literal: Chen Guan, styled Zijiang, was a man of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan, courtesy name Zijiang, was a native of Luling.

sentences.zh: 元末，世將亂，環所居築場種樹，人莫能測。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan, when the age was about to fall into disorder, he enclosed his residence, built an enclosure, and planted trees; no one could fathom his purpose.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan, sensing that the world was about to descend into chaos, he enclosed his home, built a compound, and planted trees—no one could guess why.

sentences.zh: 後十年，盜蜂起。

translations.literal: Ten years later, bandits swarmed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later, bandits rose everywhere.

sentences.zh: 灌率武勇結屯林中，盜不敢入，一鄉賴以全。

translations.literal: Guan led the brave and martial to form an encampment in the woods; bandits dared not enter, and the whole township was preserved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Guan gathered the able-bodied and formed a camp in the woods; bandits dared not enter, and the entire township was spared.

sentences.zh: 太祖平武昌，灌詣軍門謁見。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor pacified Wuchang, Guan went to the army gate to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hongwu Emperor pacified Wuchang, Guan went to the military headquarters to present himself.

sentences.zh: 與語奇之，擢湖廣行省員外郎，累遷大都督府經歷。

translations.literal: Speaking with him, the emperor found him remarkable and promoted him to assistant commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, then repeatedly transferred to administrator of the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found him remarkable in conversation and appointed him assistant commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, later promoting him repeatedly until he became administrator of the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍徐達北征。

translations.literal: He followed the great general Xu Da on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the great general Xu Da on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋命築城泰州，工竣，除甯國知府。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to build the walls of Taizhou; when the work was completed, he was appointed prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to build the walls of Taizhou, and upon completion was appointed prefect of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 時天下初定，民棄《詩》《書》久。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had just been settled, and the people had long abandoned the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had only just been pacified, and the people had long neglected learning.

sentences.zh: 灌建學舍，延師，選俊秀子弟受業。

translations.literal: Guan built schoolhouses, invited teachers, and selected outstanding young men to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Guan built schoolhouses, hired teachers, and selected promising youths to study.

sentences.zh: 訪問疾苦，禁豪右兼併。

translations.literal: He inquired into hardships and forbade powerful families from engrossing land.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated the people's hardships and prohibited powerful families from seizing land.

sentences.zh: 創戶帖以便稽民。

translations.literal: He created household registers to facilitate checking the population.
translations.idiomatic: He devised household registers to facilitate population registration.

sentences.zh: 帝取為式，頒行天下。

translations.literal: The emperor took it as a model and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted it as a model and issued it throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 伐石築堤，作水門蓄泄，護瀕江田，百姓咸賴。

translations.literal: He quarried stone to build dikes, made sluice gates for storage and release, protected fields along the river, and the common people all relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: He quarried stone to build dikes and sluice gates for irrigation and drainage, protecting riverside fields on which the people all depended.

sentences.zh: 有坐盜麥舟者，論死數十人。

translations.literal: There were those convicted of stealing grain from a drifting boat; dozens were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of people were sentenced to death for stealing grain from a drifting boat.

sentences.zh: 灌覆按曰：「舟自漂至，而愚民哄取之，非謀劫也。」

translations.literal: Guan reviewed the case and said: "The boat drifted here on its own, and foolish common people took it in a rush—it was not a planned robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Guan reviewed the case and said: "The boat drifted here on its own, and foolish villagers seized the grain in a scramble—it was not a planned robbery.

sentences.zh: 坐其首一人，餘悉減死。

translations.literal: He punished only the ringleader; the rest all had their death sentences reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He punished only the ringleader; the rest had their sentences reduced.

sentences.zh: 灌豐裁嚴正，而為治寬恤類此。

translations.literal: Guan was imposing and stern in bearing, yet in governing he was lenient and compassionate in cases like this.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was imposing and stern in manner, yet he governed with leniency and compassion in cases such as this.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年召入京，病卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was summoned to the capital and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongwu (1371) he was summoned to the capital, where he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 方克勤，字去矜，寧海人。

translations.literal: Fang Keqin, styled Qujin, was a man of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Keqin, courtesy name Qujin, was a native of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 元末，台州盜起，吳江同知金剛奴奉行省命，募水兵禦之。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan, bandits rose in Taizhou; Wujiang vice-prefect Jingangnu, carrying out the Branch Secretariat's order, recruited naval troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan, bandits rose in Taizhou; Jingangnu, vice-prefect of Wujiang, following provincial orders, recruited naval troops to resist them.

sentences.zh: 克勤獻策弗納，逃之山中。

translations.literal: Keqin offered stratagems that were not adopted and fled to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Keqin offered strategies that were rejected and fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 洪武二年辟縣訓導，母老辭歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongwu he was recruited as county instructor but declined and returned home because his mother was elderly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongwu (1369) he was recruited as county instructor but declined and returned home because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 四年征至京師，吏部試第二，特授濟甯知府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned to the capital; in the Ministry of Personnel examination he placed second and was specially appointed prefect of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1371) he was summoned to the capital, placed second in the Ministry of Personnel examination, and was specially appointed prefect of Jining.

sentences.zh: 時始詔民墾荒，閱三歲乃稅。

translations.literal: At that time an edict had just ordered the people to reclaim wasteland; only after three years would tax be levied.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had just ordered the people to reclaim wasteland, with tax to be levied only after three years.

sentences.zh: 吏征率不俟期，民謂詔旨不信，輒棄去，田復荒。

translations.literal: Officials collecting taxes generally did not wait for the term; the people said the imperial edict was untrustworthy and would abandon the land, and the fields became waste again.
translations.idiomatic: Tax collectors generally did not wait for the three-year term; the people concluded the edict was unreliable and abandoned their fields, which reverted to wasteland.

sentences.zh: 克勤與民約，稅如期。

translations.literal: Keqin made a pact with the people that tax would be collected on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Keqin pledged to the people that taxes would be collected only when due.

sentences.zh: 區田為九等，以差等徵發，吏不得為奸，野以日辟。

translations.literal: He divided fields into nine grades and levied according to differential rates; officials could not commit fraud, and the wasteland was daily opened.
translations.idiomatic: He classified fields into nine grades and levied taxes accordingly; officials could no longer cheat, and wasteland was steadily reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 又立社學數百區，葺孔子廟堂，教化興起。

translations.literal: He also established several hundred community schools and repaired the Confucian temple hall; education and transformation flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He also established hundreds of community schools and restored the Confucian temple; education flourished.

sentences.zh: 盛夏，守將督民夫築城，克勤曰：「民方耕耘不暇，奈何重困之畚鍤。」

translations.literal: In midsummer the garrison commander pressed the people into corvée to build walls; Keqin said: "The people are busy with plowing and have no spare time—how can we further burden them with shovels and baskets?
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer the garrison commander pressed the people into corvée to build walls; Keqin said: "The people are busy with the harvest and have no spare time—how can we further burden them with construction labor?

sentences.zh: 請之中書省，得罷役。

translations.literal: He petitioned the Central Secretariat and obtained cancellation of the corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the Central Secretariat and had the corvée cancelled.

sentences.zh: 先是久旱，遂大澍。

translations.literal: Before this there had been long drought; then came heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: There had been a long drought; then came a great downpour.

sentences.zh: 濟寧人歌之曰：「孰罷我役？

translations.literal: The people of Jining sang, saying: "Who ended our corvée?
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jining sang: "Who ended our corvée?

sentences.zh: 使君之力。

translations.literal: The prefect's power.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect's power.

sentences.zh: 孰活我黍？

translations.literal: Who revived our grain?
translations.idiomatic: Who revived our grain?

sentences.zh: 使君之雨。

translations.literal: The prefect's rain.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect's rain.

sentences.zh: 使君勿去，我民父母。」

translations.literal: Prefect, do not leave us—we are your children, you our parents.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect, do not leave us—you are the father and mother of your people.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，戶口增數倍，一郡饒足。

translations.literal: After three years in office, the registered population increased severalfold and the whole prefecture was prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office, the registered population increased severalfold and the entire prefecture prospered.

sentences.zh: 克勤為治，以德化為本，不喜近名，嘗曰：「近名必立威，立威必殃民，吾不忍也。」

translations.literal: Keqin in governing took moral transformation as the foundation and did not like pursuing reputation; he once said: "Pursuing reputation necessarily means establishing awe; establishing awe necessarily harms the people—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Keqin governed through moral transformation and disdained pursuing reputation; he once said: "Pursuing reputation means establishing fear; establishing fear harms the people—I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 自奉簡素，一布袍十年不易，日不再肉食。

translations.literal: His own conduct was simple and frugal; one cloth robe he did not change for ten years, and he did not eat meat twice in a day.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply and frugally, wearing the same cloth robe for ten years and eating meat no more than once a day.

sentences.zh: 太祖用法嚴，士大夫多被謫，過濟寧者，克勤輒周恤之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor applied the law strictly; many scholar-officials were banished, and those passing through Jining Keqin would always provide for them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor applied the law strictly, and many scholar-officials were banished; Keqin always provided for those passing through Jining.

sentences.zh: 永嘉侯硃亮祖嘗率舟師赴北平，水涸，役夫五千浚河。

translations.literal: Marquis Zhu Liangzu of Yongjia once led a naval force north to Beiping; when the water dried up, five thousand laborers were pressed to dredge the river.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhu Liangzu of Yongjia once led a naval force north to Beiping; when the river ran dry, five thousand laborers were pressed to dredge it.

sentences.zh: 克勤不能止，泣禱於天。

translations.literal: Keqin could not stop it and wept, praying to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Keqin could not stop it and wept, praying to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 忽大雨，水深數尺，舟遂達，民以為神。

translations.literal: Suddenly heavy rain fell, the water was several feet deep, and the boats were able to pass; the people regarded it as miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a great rain fell, the water rose several feet, and the boats passed through; the people regarded it as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 八年入朝，太祖嘉其績，賜宴，遣還郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered court; the founding emperor praised his achievements, gave a banquet, and sent him back to his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1375) he went to court; the Hongwu Emperor praised his achievements, gave a banquet, and sent him back to his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋為屬吏程貢所誣，謫役江浦，復以空印事連，逮死。

translations.literal: Soon he was slandered by his subordinate Cheng Gong, sentenced to corvée at Jiangpu, and again implicated in the empty-seal affair; he was arrested and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was slandered by his subordinate Cheng Gong and sentenced to corvée at Jiangpu; he was then implicated in the empty-seal affair, arrested, and died.

sentences.zh: 子孝聞、孝孺。

translations.literal: His sons were Xiaowen and Xiaoru.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xiaowen and Xiaoru.

sentences.zh: 孝聞，十三喪母，蔬食終制。

translations.literal: Xiaowen, at thirteen when his mother died, ate only vegetables throughout the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen, at thirteen when his mother died, ate only vegetables throughout the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 孝孺，自有傳。

translations.literal: Xiaoru has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoru has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 吳履，字德基，蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Wu Lü, styled Deji, was a man of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lü, courtesy name Deji, was a native of Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 少受業于聞人夢吉，通《春秋》諸史。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Wenren Mengji and mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and various histories.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Wenren Mengji and mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals and various histories.

sentences.zh: 李文忠鎮浙東，聘為郡學正。

translations.literal: When Li Wenzhong governed eastern Zhejiang, he was engaged as director of the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Wenzhong governed eastern Zhejiang, he was engaged as director of the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 久之，舉於朝，授南康丞。

translations.literal: After a time he was recommended to court and appointed assistant magistrate of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was recommended to court and appointed assistant magistrate of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 南康俗悍，謂丞儒也，易之。

translations.literal: Nankang customs were fierce; they said the assistant was a mere scholar and looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Nankang had a fierce populace; they assumed the assistant magistrate was a mere scholar and looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 居數月，摘發奸伏如老獄吏，則皆大驚，相率斂跡。

translations.literal: After several months he uncovered hidden wrongdoing like an old prison official; all were greatly alarmed and in succession restrained their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he uncovered hidden wrongdoing like a veteran jailer; all were greatly alarmed and restrained their conduct.

sentences.zh: 履乃改崇寬大，與民休息。

translations.literal: Lü then changed to esteem leniency and magnanimity, giving the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Lü then adopted a policy of leniency and magnanimity, giving the people rest.

sentences.zh: 知縣周以中巡視田野，為部民所詈。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zhou Yizhong was inspecting the fields when he was cursed by a local resident.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhou Yizhong was inspecting the fields when a local resident cursed him.

sentences.zh: 捕之不獲，怒，盡縶其鄉鄰。

translations.literal: Unable to capture the offender, he grew angry and arrested all the neighbors in the hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to capture the offender, he grew angry and arrested all the neighbors in the hamlet.

sentences.zh: 履閱獄問故，立釋之，乃白以中。

translations.literal: Lü reviewed the prisoners and asked the reason, immediately released them, and then reported to Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lü reviewed the prisoners, asked the reason, immediately released them, and then reported to Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 以中益怒，曰：「丞慢我。」

translations.literal: Yizhong grew even angrier and said: "The assistant disrespects me.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong grew even angrier and said: "The assistant disrespects me.

sentences.zh: 履曰：「犯公者一人耳，其鄰何罪？

translations.literal: Lü said: "Only one person offended you—what crime have the neighbors committed?
translations.idiomatic: Lü said: "Only one person offended you—what crime have the neighbors committed?

sentences.zh: 今縶者眾，而捕未已，急且有變，奈何？」

translations.literal: Now many are imprisoned while the capture is not yet complete; in urgency there may soon be trouble—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Many are imprisoned while the culprit remains at large; in their desperation they may soon rebel—what then?"

sentences.zh: 以中意乃解。

translations.literal: Yizhong's mind was then relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong's anger then subsided.

sentences.zh: 邑有淫祠，每祀輒有蛇出戶，民指為神。

translations.literal: In the district there was an illicit shrine; at every sacrifice a snake would emerge from the door, and the people pointed to it as divine.
translations.idiomatic: In the district there was an illicit shrine; at every sacrifice a snake would emerge from the door, and the people regarded it as divine.

sentences.zh: 履縛巫責之，沉神像于江，淫祠遂絕。

translations.literal: Lü bound the shaman and held him accountable, sank the divine image in the river, and illicit shrines were thereby ended.
translations.idiomatic: Lü bound the shaman and held him accountable, sank the idol in the river, and illicit shrines were abolished.

sentences.zh: 為丞六年，百姓愛之。

translations.literal: After six years as assistant, the common people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: After six years as assistant magistrate, the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 遷安化知縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Anhua.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be magistrate of Anhua.

sentences.zh: 大姓易氏保險自守，江陰侯吳良將擊之，召履計事。

translations.literal: The great clan the Yis held a fortified position and defended themselves; Marquis Wu Liang of Jiangyin was about to attack them and summoned Lü to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful Yi clan held a fortified position in self-defense; Marquis Wu Liang of Jiangyin was about to attack them and summoned Lü to discuss strategy.

sentences.zh: 履曰：「易氏逃死耳，非反也，招之當來。

translations.literal: Lü said: "The Yi clan are merely fleeing death, not rebelling; if summoned they will come.
translations.idiomatic: Lü said: "The Yi clan are merely fleeing for their lives, not rebelling; if summoned they will come.

sentences.zh: 不來，誅未晚。」

translations.literal: If they do not come, execution will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not come, punishment will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 良從之，易氏果至。

translations.literal: Liang followed this advice, and the Yi clan indeed came.
translations.idiomatic: Liang followed his advice, and the Yi clan indeed came.

sentences.zh: 良欲籍農故為兵者，民大恐。

translations.literal: Liang wished to register those who had formerly been soldiers among the farmers; the people were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Liang wished to register former soldiers among the farmers; the people were greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 履曰：「世清矣，民安于農。

translations.literal: Lü said: "The age is now peaceful; the people are secure in farming.
translations.idiomatic: Lü said: "The realm is now at peace; the people are secure in farming.

sentences.zh: 請籍其願為兵者，不願，可勿強。」

translations.literal: Please register only those willing to be soldiers; those unwilling need not be forced.
translations.idiomatic: Register only those willing to serve as soldiers; those unwilling need not be forced.

sentences.zh: 遷濰州知州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 山東兵常以牛羊代秋稅，履與民計曰：「牛羊有死瘠患，不若輸粟便。」

translations.literal: In Shandong soldiers often used cattle and sheep in place of autumn grain tax; Lü calculated with the people and said: "Cattle and sheep have the risk of death and emaciation—it is better to pay grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong soldiers often paid autumn grain tax in cattle and sheep; Lü calculated with the people and said: "Cattle and sheep risk death and disease—it is better to pay in grain.

sentences.zh: 他日，上官令民送牛羊之陝西，他縣民多破家，濰民獨完。

translations.literal: Another day superiors ordered the people to send cattle and sheep to Shaanxi; in other counties many families were ruined, but the people of Wei alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Later superiors ordered the people to send cattle and sheep to Shaanxi; in other counties many families were ruined, but the people of Wei alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 會改州為縣，召履還，濰民皆涕泣奔送。

translations.literal: When the prefecture was changed to a county, Lü was summoned back; the people of Wei all wept and ran to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture was reduced to a county, Lü was summoned back; the people of Wei all wept and ran to see him off.

sentences.zh: 履遂乞骸骨歸。

translations.literal: Lü then requested to retire on account of age and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Lü then requested retirement and returned home.

sentences.zh: 是時河內丞廖欽並以廉能稱。

translations.literal: At this time Liao Qin, assistant magistrate of Henei, was also known for incorruptibility and ability.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Liao Qin, assistant magistrate of Henei, was also known for probity and competence.

sentences.zh: 居八年，調吳江，後坐事謫戍。

translations.literal: After eight years in office he was transferred to Wujiang; later he was implicated in an affair and banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in office he was transferred to Wujiang; later he was implicated in an affair and banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 久之，以老病放歸。

translations.literal: After a long time he was released and sent home on account of old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was released and sent home on account of old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 道河內，河內民競持羊酒為壽，且遺之縑，須臾裒數百匹。

translations.literal: Passing by Henei, the people of Henei competed to present sheep and wine to wish long life, and moreover bestowed silk upon him; in an instant several hundred bolts were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Henei, the people of Henei competed to offer sheep and wine for longevity, and also gave him silk; in a moment several hundred bolts were gathered.

sentences.zh: 欽固辭不得，一夕遁去。

translations.literal: Qin firmly declined but could not; in one night he fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Qin firmly declined but could not; in one night he fled.

sentences.zh: 他若興化丞周舟以績最，特擢吏部主事。

translations.literal: Others such as Zhou Zhou, assistant magistrate of Xinghua, for the highest performance record, was specially promoted to chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise, Xinghua assistant magistrate Zhou Zhou, for top performance, was specially promoted to chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 民爭乞留，乃遣還之。

translations.literal: The people competed in begging to retain him; then he was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The people competed to beg that he stay, and he was sent back.

sentences.zh: 歸安丞高彬、曹縣主簿劉鬱、衡山主簿紀惟正、沾化典史杜濩皆坐事，以部民乞宥，復其官，而惟正立擢陝西參議。

translations.literal: Gui'an assistant magistrate Gao Bin, Cao County chief clerk Liu Yu, Hengshan chief clerk Ji Weizheng, and Zhanhua registry clerk Du Bo were all implicated in affairs; upon the local populace begging pardon, their offices were restored, and Weizheng was immediately promoted to Shaanxi Assistant Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Gui'an assistant magistrate Gao Bin, Cao County chief clerk Liu Yu, Hengshan chief clerk Ji Weizheng, and Zhanhua registry clerk Du Bo were all implicated in affairs; upon petition by the local populace for pardon, their offices were restored, and Weizheng was immediately promoted to Shaanxi Assistant Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其後州縣之佐貳知名者，在仁、宣時則易州判官張友聞、壽州判官許敏、許州判官王通、靈璧丞田誠、安平丞耿福緣、嘉定丞戴肅、大名丞賀禎、昌邑主簿劉整、襄垣主簿喬育、貴池典史黃金蘭、深澤典史高聞；

translations.literal: Later, among famous deputies and assistants of prefectures and counties, during the reigns of Renzong and Xuanzong there were Yizhou Assistant Prefect Zhang Youwen, Shouzhou Assistant Prefect Xu Min, Xuzhou Assistant Prefect Wang Tong, Lingbi Assistant Magistrate Tian Cheng, Anping Assistant Magistrate Geng Fuyuan, Jiading Assistant Magistrate Dai Su, Daming Assistant Magistrate He Zhen, Changyi Chief Clerk Liu Zheng, Xiangyuan Chief Clerk Qiao Yu, Guichi Registry Clerk Huang Jinlan, and Shenze Registry Clerk Gao Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Later, among the well-known deputies and assistants of prefectures and counties, during the reigns of Renzong and Xuanzong there were Yizhou Assistant Prefect Zhang Youwen, Shouzhou Assistant Prefect Xu Min, Xuzhou Assistant Prefect Wang Tong, Lingbi Assistant Magistrate Tian Cheng, Anping Assistant Magistrate Geng Fuyuan, Jiading Assistant Magistrate Dai Su, Daming Assistant Magistrate He Zhen, Changyi Chief Clerk Liu Zheng, Xiangyuan Chief Clerk Qiao Yu, Guichi Registry Clerk Huang Jinlan, and Shenze Registry Clerk Gao Wen;

sentences.zh: 英、景時則養利判官汪浩、泰州判官王思旻、上海丞張禎、吳江丞王懋本、曆城丞熊觀、黔陽主簿古初、雲南南安州琅井巡檢李保。

translations.literal: During the reigns of the Yingzong and Jingtai Emperors there were Yangli Assistant Prefect Wang Hao, Taizhou Assistant Prefect Wang Simin, Shanghai Assistant Magistrate Zhang Zhen, Wujiang Assistant Magistrate Wang Maoben, Licheng Assistant Magistrate Xiong Guan, Qianyang Chief Clerk Gu Chu, and Li Bao, Langjing postal inspector of Nan'an Prefecture, Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of the Yingzong and Jingtai Emperors there were Yangli Assistant Prefect Wang Hao, Taizhou Assistant Prefect Wang Simin, Shanghai Assistant Magistrate Zhang Zhen, Wujiang Assistant Magistrate Wang Maoben, Licheng Assistant Magistrate Xiong Guan, Qianyang Chief Clerk Gu Chu, and Li Bao, Langjing postal inspector of Nan'an Prefecture, Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 或超遷，或遷任，皆因部民請雲。

translations.literal: Some were promoted out of turn, some were transferred in post—all upon the local populace's request.
translations.idiomatic: Some were promoted out of turn, some were transferred in place—all upon petition by the local populace.

sentences.zh: 高鬥南，字拱極，陝西徽州人。

translations.literal: Gao Dounan, courtesy name Gongji, was a native of Huizhou, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dounan, courtesy name Gongji, was a native of Huizhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 貌魁梧，語音若鐘。

translations.literal: His appearance was stalwart; his voice was like a bell.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing, and his voice rang like a bell.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，由薦舉授四川定遠知縣。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, through recommendation he was appointed magistrate of Dingyuan in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign, on recommendation he was appointed magistrate of Dingyuan in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 才識精敏，多善政。

translations.literal: His talent and insight were keen and sharp; he had many good policies.
translations.idiomatic: Keen in talent and judgment, he enacted many good policies.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，與知府永州余彥誠，知縣齊東鄭敏、儀真康彥民、岳池王佐、安肅範志遠、當塗孟廉及丞懷甯蘇億、休甯甘鏞、當塗趙森並坐事，先後被征。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, together with Yongzhou Prefect Yu Yancheng, magistrates Zheng Min of Qidong, Kang Yanmin of Yizhen, Wang Zuo of Yuechi, Fan Zhiyuan of Ansu, and Meng Lian of Dangtu, and assistant magistrates Su Yi of Huaining, Gan Yong of Xiuning, and Zhao Sen of Dangtu, he was implicated in affairs and, one after another, was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, together with Yongzhou Prefect Yu Yancheng, magistrates Zheng Min of Qidong, Kang Yanmin of Yizhen, Wang Zuo of Yuechi, Fan Zhiyuan of Ansu, and Meng Lian of Dangtu, and assistant magistrates Su Yi of Huaining, Gan Yong of Xiuning, and Zhao Sen of Dangtu, he was implicated in affairs and summoned to the capital in turn.

sentences.zh: 其耆民奔走闕下，具列善政以聞。

translations.literal: Their elderly residents rushed to the capital gate, fully listing good policies to report.
translations.idiomatic: Their elders rushed to the capital, itemizing their good policies and reporting them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，賜襲衣寶鈔遣還，並賜耆民道路費。

translations.literal: The Hongwu Emperor commended this, bestowed court robes and paper money and sent them back, and also bestowed travel expenses on the elders.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor commended them, bestowed court robes and paper money, and sent them back, also granting the elders travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 諸人既還任，政績益著。

translations.literal: Once these men had returned to their posts, their administrative achievements became even more outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Once they returned to office, their achievements became even more outstanding.

sentences.zh: 尋舉天下廉吏數人，鬥南與焉，列其名於《彰善榜》、《聖政記》以示勸。

translations.literal: Soon several incorrupt officials under Heaven were selected; Dounan was among them, and their names were listed in the Register of Goodness Displayed and the Record of Sagely Governance to show encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon several incorrupt officials throughout the realm were selected; Dounan was among them, and their names were listed in the Register of Goodness Displayed and the Record of Sagely Governance as encouragement to others.

sentences.zh: 九載績最，擢雲南新興知州，新興人愛之不異定遠。

translations.literal: After nine years with the highest performance record, he was promoted to prefect of Xinxing in Yunnan; the people of Xinxing loved him no less than those of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years with the top performance record, he was promoted to prefect of Xinxing in Yunnan; the people of Xinxing loved him no less than those of Dingyuan had.

sentences.zh: 居數年，以衰老乞歸，薦子吏科給事中恂自代，成祖許之。

translations.literal: After several years in office, he requested retirement on account of old age, recommended his son Xun, a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel, to replace him, and the Yongle Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he requested retirement on account of old age, recommending his son Xun, a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel, to succeed him; the Yongle Emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 年七十而卒。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 恂，字士信，博學能詩文。

translations.literal: Xun, courtesy name Shixin, was broadly learned and skilled in poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, courtesy name Shixin, was broadly learned and accomplished in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 官新興，從大軍征交址，有協贊功。

translations.literal: Serving as prefect of Xinxing, he followed the great army in the campaign against Jiaozhi and had meritorious service in assisting.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Xinxing, he followed the main army in the campaign against Jiaozhi and rendered meritorious assistance.

sentences.zh: 師旋，卒於官。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 彥誠，德興人。

translations.literal: Yancheng was a native of Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: Yancheng was a native of Dexing.

sentences.zh: 初知安陸州，以徵稅愆期，當就逮，其父老伏闕乞留。

translations.literal: At first he was magistrate of Anlu Prefecture; because tax collection was overdue he was to be arrested; the elders of the district prostrated themselves at the gate begging to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as magistrate of Anlu Prefecture; because tax collection was overdue he was to be arrested, but the district elders prostrated themselves at the palace gate begging that he be retained.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜宴嘉賞，遣還，父老亦預宴。

translations.literal: The Hongwu Emperor bestowed a banquet and commendation, sent him back, and the elders also attended the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor granted a banquet and commendation and sent him back; the elders were also invited to the banquet.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢知永州府，終河東鹽運使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to prefect of Yongzhou and ended as salt transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was promoted to prefect of Yongzhou and ended his career as Hedong salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 敏，常坐事被逮，部民數千人守闕下求宥。

translations.literal: Min was often implicated in affairs and arrested; several thousand local populace kept watch at the capital gate seeking pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Min was often implicated in affairs and arrested; several thousand local populace kept vigil at the palace gate seeking his pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝宴勞，復其官，賜鈔百錠，衣三襲。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted and rewarded them, restored his office, and bestowed one hundred ingots of paper money and three suits of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted and rewarded them, restored his office, and bestowed one hundred ingots of paper money and three suits of clothing.

sentences.zh: 居數年，考滿入朝。

translations.literal: After several years in office, when his term review was complete he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: After several years, when his term review was complete, he came to court.

sentences.zh: 部民復走京師，乞再任，帝從其請。

translations.literal: The local populace again went to the capital, begging for another term; the emperor granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: The local populace again went to the capital begging for another term, and the emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 及是，再獲宥。

translations.literal: At this time he was again granted pardon.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he was again granted pardon.

sentences.zh: 彥民，泰和人。

translations.literal: Yanmin was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Yanmin was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was a jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 先知青田，調儀真，後曆巴陵、天臺，並著名績。

translations.literal: He first served as magistrate of Qingtian, was transferred to Yizhen, and later served successively at Baling and Tiantai, all with distinguished records.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as magistrate of Qingtian, was transferred to Yizhen, and later served at Baling and Tiantai in succession, earning distinguished records at each post.

sentences.zh: 永樂初罷歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongle reign he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，御史巡按至天臺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, an investigating censor on provincial tour arrived at Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi, an investigating censor on provincial tour arrived at Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 縣民二百餘人言彥民廉公有為，乞還之天臺，慰民望。

translations.literal: More than two hundred county residents stated that Yanmin was incorrupt, fair, and capable, begging that he be returned to Tiantai to satisfy the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred county residents reported that Yanmin was incorrupt, fair, and capable, begging that he be returned to Tiantai to satisfy the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 御史以聞，宣宗歎曰：「彥民去天臺二十餘年，民猶思之，其有善政可知。」

translations.literal: The censor reported this; the Xuanzong sighed and said: "Yanmin left Tiantai more than twenty years ago, yet the people still think of him—it can be known that he had good policies.
translations.idiomatic: The censor reported this; the Xuanzong sighed and said: "Yanmin left Tiantai more than twenty years ago, yet the people still long for him—it is clear that he governed well.

sentences.zh: 乃用為江寧縣丞。

translations.literal: He was then appointed assistant magistrate of Jiangning County.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed assistant magistrate of Jiangning County.

sentences.zh: 億、廉、森三人既釋還，明年復以事當逮。

translations.literal: Yi, Lian, and Sen—the three of them—once released and sent back, the next year were again to be arrested on account of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yi, Lian, and Sen had been released and sent back, the next year they were again to be arrested on account of affairs.

sentences.zh: 縣民又走闕下頌其廉勤，帝亦釋之。

translations.literal: County residents again went to the capital gate praising their incorruptibility and diligence; the emperor also released them.
translations.idiomatic: County residents again went to the palace gate praising their incorruptibility and diligence, and the emperor released them as well.

sentences.zh: 時太祖操重典繩群下，守令坐小過輒逮系。

translations.literal: At this time the Hongwu Emperor wielded heavy statutes to constrain his subordinates; prefects and magistrates who incurred minor faults were immediately arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Hongwu Emperor wielded severe law to restrain his subordinates; prefects and magistrates who committed minor faults were immediately arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 聞其賢，旋遣還，且加賞賚，有因以超擢者。

translations.literal: When their virtue was heard of, they were quickly sent back, moreover given rewards and gifts; some were even promoted out of turn on that account.
translations.idiomatic: When their virtue became known, they were quickly sent back and further rewarded; some were even promoted out of turn on that account.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，知縣靈璧周榮、宜春沈昌、昌樂於子仁，丞新化葉宗並坐事逮訊，部民為叩閽。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, magistrates Zhou Rong of Lingbi, Shen Chang of Yichun, and Yu Ziren of Changle, and assistant magistrate Ye Zong of Xinhua were all implicated in affairs, arrested and interrogated; the local populace knocked at the palace gate on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, magistrates Zhou Rong of Lingbi, Shen Chang of Yichun, and Yu Ziren of Changle, and Xinhua assistant magistrate Ye Zong were all implicated in affairs, arrested, and interrogated; the local populace knocked at the palace gate on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，立擢四人為知府，榮河南，昌南安，子仁登州，宗黃州。

translations.literal: The Hongwu Emperor was pleased and immediately promoted all four to prefect: Rong to Henan, Chang to Nan'an, Ziren to Dengzhou, and Zong to Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor was pleased and immediately promoted all four to prefect: Rong to Henan, Chang to Nan'an, Ziren to Dengzhou, and Zong to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 由是長吏競勸，一時多循良之績焉。

translations.literal: From this senior officials competed in encouragement, and for a time there were many achievements of virtuous officials.
translations.idiomatic: From this senior officials strove to excel, and for a time there were many achievements by virtuous officials.

sentences.zh: 榮，字國華，蓬萊人。

translations.literal: Rong, courtesy name Guohua, was a native of Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, courtesy name Guohua, was a native of Penglai.

sentences.zh: 初為靈璧丞，坐累逮下刑部，耆老群赴輦下稱其賢。

translations.literal: At first he was assistant magistrate of Lingbi; implicated through association he was arrested and sent down to the Ministry of Punishments; elders in groups went to the capital praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as assistant magistrate of Lingbi; implicated through association he was arrested and sent to the Ministry of Punishments, while elders in groups went to the capital praising his virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝賜鈔八十錠，綺羅衣各一襲。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed eighty ingots of paper money and one suit of brocade and gauze clothing to each.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed eighty ingots of paper money and one suit of brocade and gauze clothing on each.

sentences.zh: 禮部宴榮及耆老而還之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites feasted Rong and the elders, then sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites feasted Rong and the elders, then sent them home.

sentences.zh: 無何，擢榮靈璧知縣。

translations.literal: Before long Rong was promoted to magistrate of Lingbi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Rong was promoted to magistrate of Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 及知河南，亦有聲。

translations.literal: When he became prefect of Henan he also had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When he became prefect of Henan he also won a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 後建言稱旨，擢河南左布政使。

translations.literal: Later he submitted a memorial that pleased the throne and was promoted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted a memorial that pleased the throne and was promoted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 史誠祖，解州人。

translations.literal: Shi Chengzu was a native of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chengzu was a native of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，詣闕陳鹽法利弊。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu he went to the capital to set forth the advantages and disadvantages of the salt laws.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Hongwu reign he went to the capital to set forth the advantages and disadvantages of the salt laws.

sentences.zh: 太祖納之，授汶上知縣，為治廉平寬簡。

translations.literal: The Hongwu Emperor accepted his views, appointed him magistrate of Wenshang, and his governance was incorrupt, fair, lenient, and simple.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor accepted his views, appointed him magistrate of Wenshang, and his governance was incorrupt, fair, lenient, and simple.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年，成祖北巡，遣御史考核郡縣長吏賢否，還言誠祖治第一。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle, the Yongle Emperor toured the north and dispatched censors to assess whether prefectural and county chiefs were worthy or not; on returning they reported that Chengzu's governance ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongle, the Yongle Emperor toured the north and dispatched censors to assess the worth of prefectural and county chiefs; on returning they reported that Chengzu's governance ranked first.

sentences.zh: 賜璽書勞之曰：「守令承流宣化，所以安利元元。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial sealed letter commending him, which said: "Prefects and magistrates receive the stream and proclaim transformation—thereby benefiting and securing the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an imperial sealed letter of commendation, which read: "Prefects and magistrates carry imperial policy to the people and proclaim moral transformation, thereby benefiting and securing the common people.

sentences.zh: 朕統禦天下，夙夜求賢，共圖治理。

translations.literal: I rule and govern All Under Heaven, seeking the worthy day and night, jointly planning good governance.
translations.idiomatic: I rule All Under Heaven, seeking the worthy day and night, that together we may achieve good governance.

sentences.zh: 往往下詢民間，皆言苦吏苛急，能副朕心者實鮮。

translations.literal: Often when I inquire among the people below, all say they suffer from harsh and pressing officials; those who can accord with my intent are truly few.
translations.idiomatic: Often when I inquire among the people, all complain of harsh and overbearing officials; those who truly meet my expectations are indeed few.

sentences.zh: 爾敦厚老成，恪共乃職；

translations.literal: You are sincere, steady, and mature, reverently performing your duties;
translations.idiomatic: You are sincere, steady, and mature, reverently performing your duties;

sentences.zh: 持身勵志，一于廉公。

translations.literal: maintaining your person and urging your will, wholly incorrupt and fair.
translations.idiomatic: upholding yourself and urging your will, wholly incorrupt and fair.

sentences.zh: 平賦均徭，政清訟簡，民心悅戴，境內稱安。

translations.literal: You equalize levies and distribute corvée fairly; government is clear and litigation simple; the people's hearts rejoice in you, and within your jurisdiction all call it peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: You equalize levies and distribute corvée fairly; government is clear and litigation simple; the people rejoice in you, and throughout your jurisdiction all speak of peace.

sentences.zh: 方古良吏，亦復何讓。

translations.literal: Compared with virtuous officials of old, what would you yield?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with virtuous officials of old, what would you yield?

sentences.zh: 特擢爾濟寧知州，仍視汶上縣事。

translations.literal: You are specially promoted to prefect of Jining, while still overseeing the affairs of Wenshang County.
translations.idiomatic: You are specially promoted to prefect of Jining, while still overseeing the affairs of Wenshang County.

sentences.zh: 其益共乃職，慎終如始，以永嘉譽，欽哉。」

translations.literal: Further reverently perform your duties, be as careful at the end as at the beginning, thereby forever maintaining good repute—reverently so!
translations.idiomatic: Continue reverently in your duties, be as careful at the end as at the beginning, and thereby preserve your good name forever. Take heed!

sentences.zh: 並賜內醞一尊，織金紗衣一襲，鈔千貫。

translations.literal: A jar of imperial wine, one suit of woven-gold gauze clothing, and one thousand strings of paper money were also bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: A jar of imperial wine, one suit of woven-gold gauze clothing, and one thousand strings of paper money were also bestowed.

sentences.zh: 御史又言貪吏虐民無若易州同知張騰，遂征下獄。

translations.literal: The censor further reported that no corrupt official oppressed the people like Zhang Teng, Vice Prefect of Yizhou; he was therefore summoned and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The censor further reported that no corrupt official oppressed the people like Zhang Teng, Vice Prefect of Yizhou; he was therefore summoned and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 誠祖既得旌，益勤於治。

translations.literal: Once Chengzu had received this commendation, he was all the more diligent in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chengzu had received this commendation, he was all the more diligent in governance.

sentences.zh: 土田增辟，戶口繁滋，益編戶十四里。

translations.literal: Arable land was further opened up, households and population flourished, and fourteen additional registered communities were added.
translations.idiomatic: Arable land was further opened up, households and population flourished, and fourteen additional registered communities were added.

sentences.zh: 成祖過汶上，欲徙其民數百家於膠州，誠祖奏免之。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor passed through Wenshang, he wished to relocate several hundred of its households to Jiaozhou; Chengzu memorialized and secured exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor passed through Wenshang, he wished to relocate several hundred of its households to Jiaozhou; Chengzu memorialized and secured exemption.

sentences.zh: 屢當遷職，輒為民奏留。

translations.literal: Repeatedly when he was due for transfer, the people memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly when he was due for transfer, the people memorialized to retain him.

sentences.zh: 閱二十九年，竟卒于任。

translations.literal: After twenty-nine years he finally died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-nine years he finally died in office.

sentences.zh: 士民哀號，留葬城南，歲時奉祀。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners wailed in grief, had him buried south of the city, and offered sacrifices at seasonal times.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners wailed in grief, had him buried south of the city, and offered sacrifices at the seasonal festivals.

sentences.zh: 是時，縣令多久任。

translations.literal: At this time county magistrates often served long terms.
translations.idiomatic: At this time county magistrates often served long terms.

sentences.zh: 蠡縣吳祥，永樂時知嵩縣，至宣德中，閱三十二年卒于任。

translations.literal: Wu Xiang of Li County served as magistrate of Song County from the Yongle reign until the Xuande reign, spanning thirty-two years before dying in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiang of Li County served as magistrate of Song County from the Yongle reign until the Xuande reign, a span of thirty-two years, before dying in office.

sentences.zh: 臨汾李信，永樂時由國子生授遵化知縣，至宣德中，閱二十七年始擢無為知州。

translations.literal: Li Xin of Linfen, appointed magistrate of Zunhua from a Guozijian student during Yongle, after twenty-seven years was finally promoted to prefect of Wuwei during Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin of Linfen, appointed magistrate of Zunhua from among Guozijian students during Yongle, after twenty-seven years was finally promoted to prefect of Wuwei during Xuande.

sentences.zh: 以年老不欲赴，遂乞歸。

translations.literal: On account of old age he did not wish to go; he then requested to retire.
translations.idiomatic: On account of old age he did not wish to go, and so requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 涓縣房岩，宣德間為鄒縣知縣，至正統中，閱二十餘年卒于任，吏民皆愛戴之。

translations.literal: Fang Yan of Juan County served as magistrate of Zou County from the Xuande period until the Zhengtong period, spanning more than twenty years before dying in office; officials and commoners all loved and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yan of Juan County served as magistrate of Zou County from the Xuande period until the Zhengtong period, a span of more than twenty years, before dying in office; officials and commoners all loved and honored him.

sentences.zh: 而吉水知縣武進錢本忠有廉名，詿誤罷官。

translations.literal: Qian Benzhong of Wujin, magistrate of Jishui, had a reputation for incorruptibility but was dismissed on account of an entangling error.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Benzhong of Wujin, magistrate of Jishui, had a reputation for incorruptibility but was dismissed on account of an entangling error.

sentences.zh: 父老奔走，號泣乞留，郡人胡廣力保之，得還任。

translations.literal: Elders rushed about weeping and begging to retain him; Hu Guang of the prefecture forcefully vouched for him, and he was able to return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Elders rushed about weeping and begging to retain him; Hu Guang of the prefecture forcefully vouched for him, and he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 民聞本忠復來，空閭井迎拜。

translations.literal: When the people heard Benzhong was returning, they emptied lanes and alleys to welcome and bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard Benzhong was returning, they emptied the lanes and alleys to welcome and bow to him.

sentences.zh: 永樂中卒官，民哀慕，留葬吉水，爭負土營墳，其得民如誠祖雲。

translations.literal: He died in office during Yongle; the people mourned and admired him, had him buried in Jishui, and competed to carry earth to build his tomb—the extent to which he won the people was like Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office during Yongle; the people mourned and admired him, had him buried in Jishui, and competed to carry earth to build his tomb—the extent to which he won the people was like Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 謝子襄，名袞，以字行，新淦人。

translations.literal: Xie Zixiang, given name Gun, was known by his courtesy name; he was a native of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zixiang, given name Gun, was known by his courtesy name; he was a native of Xingan.

sentences.zh: 建文中，由薦舉授青田知縣。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, through recommendation he was appointed magistrate of Qingtian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign, on recommendation he was appointed magistrate of Qingtian.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年，與錢塘知縣黃信中、開化知縣夏升並九載課最，當遷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongle, together with Huang Xixin, magistrate of Qiantang, and Xia Sheng, magistrate of Kaihua, after nine years with the highest evaluation records, they were due for transfer.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongle, together with Huang Xixin, magistrate of Qiantang, and Xia Sheng, magistrate of Kaihua, after nine years with the top evaluation records, they were due for transfer.

sentences.zh: 其部民相率訴于上官，乞再任，上官以聞。

translations.literal: Their local populace went in groups to appeal to superiors, begging for another term; the superiors reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Their local populace went in groups to appeal to their superiors, begging for another term; the superiors reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，即擢子襄處州知府，信中杭州，升衢州，俾得治其故縣。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this and immediately promoted Zixiang to prefect of Chuzhou, Xixin to Hangzhou, and Sheng to Quzhou, enabling them to govern their former counties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended this and immediately promoted Zixiang to prefect of Chuzhou, Xixin to Hangzhou, and Sheng to Quzhou, enabling them to govern their former counties.

sentences.zh: 子襄治處州，聲績益著。

translations.literal: Zixiang governed Chuzhou, and his reputation and achievements became even more outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang governed Chuzhou, and his reputation and achievements became even more outstanding.

sentences.zh: 郡有虎患。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a tiger scourge.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture suffered from tigers.

sentences.zh: 歲旱蝗。

translations.literal: That year there was drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: That year there was drought and locusts.

sentences.zh: 禱于神，大雨二日，蝗盡死，虎亦循去。

translations.literal: He prayed to the gods; great rain fell for two days, the locusts all died, and the tiger also departed along its way.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed to the gods; heavy rain fell for two days, the locusts all died, and the tiger also departed.

sentences.zh: 有盜竊官鈔，子襄檄城隍神。

translations.literal: There was a thief who stole official paper money; Zixiang issued a writ to the City God.
translations.idiomatic: When someone stole official paper money, Zixiang issued a writ to the City God.

sentences.zh: 盜方閱鈔密室，忽疾風卷墮市中，盜即伏罪。

translations.literal: The thief was just examining the notes in a secret room when suddenly a fierce wind rolled them and dropped them in the market; the thief immediately confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was just examining the notes in a secret room when suddenly a fierce wind swept them up and dropped them in the market; the thief immediately confessed.

sentences.zh: 民鬻牛於市，將屠之。

translations.literal: A man was selling an ox in the market, about to slaughter it.
translations.idiomatic: A man was selling an ox in the market, about to slaughter it.

sentences.zh: 牛逸至子襄前，俯首若有訴，乃捐俸贖還其主。

translations.literal: The ox escaped to before Zixiang, lowered its head as if pleading; he then donated his salary to redeem it and return it to its owner.
translations.idiomatic: The ox escaped to Zixiang, lowered its head as if pleading; he then donated his salary to redeem it and return it to its owner.

sentences.zh: 叛卒吳米據山谷為亂，朝廷發兵討之，一郡洶洶。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldier Wu Mi held the mountain valleys in rebellion; the court dispatched troops to suppress him, and the whole prefecture was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous soldier Wu Mi held the mountain valleys in rebellion; the court dispatched troops to suppress him, and the whole prefecture was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 子襄力止軍城中毋出，而自以計掩捕之，獲其魁，餘悉解散。

translations.literal: Zixiang forcefully stopped the army from leaving the city, and himself by stratagem captured them in ambush, seizing their leader; the rest all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang forcefully stopped the army from leaving the city, and himself by stratagem captured the rebels in ambush, seizing their leader; the rest all dispersed.

sentences.zh: 為人廉謹，曆官三十年，不以家累自隨。

translations.literal: As a man he was incorrupt and careful; over thirty years in office he did not bring his household dependents with him.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was incorrupt and careful; over thirty years in office he did not bring his household with him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yongle, he died.

sentences.zh: 信中，餘幹人。

translations.literal: Xinzhong was a native of Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xinzhong was a native of Yugan.

sentences.zh: 先知樂清縣。

translations.literal: First he was magistrate of Yueqing County.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as magistrate of Yueqing County.

sentences.zh: 奸人紿寡婦至京，誣告鄉人謀叛，而己逸去。

translations.literal: A wicked man deceived a widow and brought her to the capital, falsely accusing a fellow townsman of plotting rebellion, while he himself escaped and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A scoundrel tricked a widow into traveling to the capital to falsely accuse a fellow townsman of plotting rebellion, then fled himself.

sentences.zh: 有司系其婦以聞，詔行所司會鞫。

translations.literal: The responsible offices detained the woman and reported it; an edict ordered the relevant offices to conduct a joint inquest.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities detained the woman and reported the matter; the throne ordered the responsible offices to conduct a joint investigation and trial.

sentences.zh: 信中廉得其情，力詆為誣，獲全者甚眾。

translations.literal: Xinzhong with incorrupt clarity obtained the true facts, strenuously denounced it as false accusation, and very many were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhong investigated with incorrupt clarity, vigorously exposed the accusation as false, and saved a great many people.

sentences.zh: 盜殺一家三人，獄久不決。

translations.literal: A robber killed three people of one household; the case long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: When a robber murdered three members of one household, the case long remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 信中禱於神，得真盜，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Xinzhong prayed to the gods, obtained the real robber, and near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhong prayed to the gods, captured the real culprit, and won acclaim near and far.

sentences.zh: 升，鹽城人。

translations.literal: Sheng was a native of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Sheng was a native of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 貝秉彝，名恒，以字行，上虞人。

translations.literal: Bei Bingyi, given name Heng, was known by his courtesy name; he was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Bingyi, given name Heng, was known by his courtesy name; he was a native of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 授邵陽知縣，以憂去，補東阿。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Shaoyang; he left on account of mourning, and was reassigned to Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Shaoyang, left office to observe mourning, and was then reassigned to Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 善決獄，能以禮義導民。

translations.literal: He was skilled at deciding cases and could guide the people through ritual and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at resolving legal cases and could guide the people through ritual and moral persuasion.

sentences.zh: 歲大侵，上平糴備荒議。

translations.literal: When the year suffered great famine, he submitted a proposal for even-price grain purchases to prepare against dearth.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe famine, he submitted a proposal for government grain purchases at fair prices to build up famine reserves.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，班下郡縣如東阿式。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it and promulgated it to the prefectures and counties according to the Dong'e model.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and promulgated the policy to prefectures and counties on the Dong'e model.

sentences.zh: 邑西南有巨浸，積潦為田害。

translations.literal: Southwest of the county seat was a great inundation; accumulated floodwaters harmed the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the county seat lay a vast flooded expanse that accumulated water and ruined the fields.

sentences.zh: 秉彝相視高下，鑿渠，引入大清河，涸之，得沃壤數百頃，民食其利。

translations.literal: Bingyi surveyed high and low, dug canals, led the water into the Daqing River, drained it, and obtained several hundred qing of fertile land; the people enjoyed its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyi surveyed the terrain, dug canals to channel the water into the Daqing River and drain the marshes, reclaiming several hundred qing of fertile land from which the people reaped the benefit.

sentences.zh: 尤善綜畫，凡廢鐵、敗皮、朽索、故紙悉藏之。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at comprehensive planning; whatever scrap iron, spoiled hides, rotted rope, or old paper there was, he stored it all.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at comprehensive planning and stored every scrap of iron, spoiled hide, rotted rope, and old paper he could find.

sentences.zh: 暇令工匠煮膠、鑄杵、搗紙、絞索貯於庫。

translations.literal: In leisure hours he had craftsmen boil glue, cast pestles, pound paper, and twist rope, storing them in the warehouse.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments he had craftsmen boil glue, cast pestles, pound paper, and twist rope, storing the products in the warehouse.

sentences.zh: 會成祖北巡，敕有司建席殿。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yongle Emperor toured the north and ordered the responsible offices to build a pavilion hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor toured the north, he ordered the local authorities to erect a reception pavilion.

sentences.zh: 秉彝出所貯濟用，工遂速竣。

translations.literal: Bingyi brought out what he had stored to supply the need, and the work was quickly completed.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyi supplied materials from his stores, and the work was quickly completed.

sentences.zh: 帝將召之，東阿耆老百余人詣闕自言，願留貝令，帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to summon him when more than a hundred elders of Dong'e went to the palace gate to speak for themselves, wishing to keep Magistrate Bei; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to summon him, more than a hundred elders of Dong'e went to the palace and petitioned to keep Magistrate Bei in office; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 九載考滿入都，詔進一階，仍還東阿。

translations.literal: After nine years his evaluation term was complete and he entered the capital; an edict advanced him one rank and still sent him back to Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years, when his term evaluation was complete, he went to the capital; the throne promoted him one rank and sent him back to Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐累，罰役京師。

translations.literal: He once incurred involvement in a case and was sentenced to corvée labor in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He once became implicated in a case and was sentenced to labor service in the capital.

sentences.zh: 民競代其役，三罰三代，乃復官。

translations.literal: The people vied to substitute for his labor; three times he was sentenced and three times they served in his place, and only then was he restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The people competed to perform his labor for him; three times he was sentenced and three times they served in his stead before he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 秉彝為吏明察而仁恕。

translations.literal: As an official Bingyi was perceptive and discerning yet benevolent and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: As an official, Bingyi was perceptive yet humane and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 素善飲，已仕，遂已之。

translations.literal: By nature he was good at drinking; once he took office, he then stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Though fond of drink by nature, he gave it up once he took office.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年卒官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzong he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuande reign, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 時龍溪知縣南昌劉孟雍、鄒縣知縣龍溪硃瑤、建安知縣昆山張准、婺源知縣建安吳春、歙縣知縣江西樂平石啟宗，皆有惠利，民率懷思不忘雲。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Mengyong of Nanchang, magistrate of Longxi; Zhu Yao of Longxi, magistrate of Zou; Zhang Zhun of Kunshan, magistrate of Jian'an; Wu Chun of Jian'an, magistrate of Wuyuan; and Shi Qizong of Leping in Jiangxi, magistrate of She County, all brought benefits to the people; the people generally cherished them in memory and never forgot them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Mengyong of Nanchang, magistrate of Longxi; Zhu Yao of Longxi, magistrate of Zou; Zhang Zhun of Kunshan, magistrate of Jian'an; Wu Chun of Jian'an, magistrate of Wuyuan; and Shi Qizong of Leping in Jiangxi, magistrate of She—all benefited the people, who cherished their memory and never forgot them.

sentences.zh: 萬觀，字經訓，南昌人。

translations.literal: Wan Guan, courtesy name Jingxun, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Guan, courtesy name Jingxun, was a native of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 弱冠成永樂十九年進士。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination in the nineteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Not yet twenty, he passed the jinshi examination in the nineteenth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 帝少之，令歸肄學。

translations.literal: The emperor thought him too young and ordered him to return and continue his studies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him too young and sent him back to continue his studies.

sentences.zh: 尋召為御史，改嚴州知府。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as censor and transferred to be prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to serve as censor, then transferred to be prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 府東境七里瀧，有漁舟數百艇，時剽行旅。

translations.literal: On the eastern border of the prefecture was Qili Long; there were several hundred fishing boats that from time to time plundered travelers.
translations.idiomatic: At Qili Long on the prefecture's eastern border, several hundred fishing boats periodically preyed on travelers.

sentences.zh: 觀編十舟為一甲，令畫地巡警。

translations.literal: Guan organized ten boats into one company and ordered them to patrol assigned areas.
translations.idiomatic: Guan organized the boats into groups of ten and assigned each group a patrol area.

sentences.zh: 不匝月，盜屏跡。

translations.literal: Before a full month, the bandits vanished without trace.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month, the bandits had vanished.

sentences.zh: 乃勵學校，勸農桑，奏減織造，以銀代絲稅，民皆便之。

translations.literal: He then encouraged the schools, exhorted agriculture and sericulture, memorialized to reduce textile levies, and substituted silver for silk tax; the people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He then revitalized the schools, encouraged farming and sericulture, memorialized to reduce textile levies, and substituted silver for silk tax—all measures the people welcomed.

sentences.zh: 九年考績，治行為海內第一。

translations.literal: At the nine-year evaluation of performance, his governance ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At his nine-year performance review, his record of governance ranked first in the empire.

sentences.zh: 既以憂去，將除服，嚴州民豫上章願復得觀為守，金、衢民亦上章乞之。

translations.literal: Having left on account of mourning, when he was about to complete mourning, the people of Yanzhou preemptively submitted memorials wishing to have Guan again as prefect; the people of Jin and Qu also submitted memorials begging for him.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office to mourn, as his mourning period neared its end, the people of Yanzhou petitioned in advance to have Guan restored as prefect, and the people of Jinhua and Quzhou petitioned as well.

sentences.zh: 朝廷異焉，補平陽府，政績益茂。

translations.literal: The court was struck by this and appointed him to Pingyang Prefecture, where his administrative achievements grew even more abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The court took note and appointed him prefect of Pingyang, where his achievements grew even more impressive.

sentences.zh: 有芝生堯祠棟上，士民皆言使君德化所致。

translations.literal: An auspicious fungus grew on the ridgepole of the Yao shrine; gentry and commoners all said it was caused by the prefect's virtuous transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When an auspicious fungus appeared on the ridgepole of the shrine to Emperor Yao, gentry and commoners alike attributed it to the prefect's virtuous governance.

sentences.zh: 觀曰：「太守知奉職而已，芝，非吾事也。」

translations.literal: Guan said: "A prefect knows only to fulfill his duties; the fungus is not my concern."
translations.idiomatic: Guan said: "A prefect knows only to fulfill his duties; the fungus is not my concern."

sentences.zh: 考滿，擢山東布政使，卒於官。

translations.literal: When his evaluation term was complete, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When his evaluation term was complete, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Shandong and died in office.

sentences.zh: 葉宗人，字宗行，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Ye Zongren, courtesy name Zongxing, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zongren, courtesy name Zongxing, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，尚書夏原吉治水東南。

translations.literal: During Yongle, Minister Xia Yuanji controlled floods in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, Minister Xia Yuanji undertook flood control in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 宗人以諸生上疏，請浚範家港引浦水入海，禁瀕海民毋作壩以遏其流。

translations.literal: Zongren as a student submitted a memorial requesting dredging of Fanjiagang to lead the Pu River's waters to the sea, and forbidding coastal people from building dams to block its flow.
translations.idiomatic: As a student, Zongren submitted a memorial proposing to dredge Fanjiagang to channel Pu River water to the sea and to forbid coastal residents from building dams that obstructed its flow.

sentences.zh: 帝令赴原吉所自效。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to go to Yuanji's office to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to report to Yuanji's office and serve there.

sentences.zh: 工竣，原吉薦之，授錢塘知縣。

translations.literal: When the project was complete, Yuanji recommended him and he was appointed magistrate of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was completed, Yuanji recommended him, and he was appointed magistrate of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 縣為浙江省會，徭重，豪有力往往構黠吏得財役貧民。

translations.literal: The county was the provincial capital of Zhejiang; corvée was heavy, and powerful magnates often colluded with cunning clerks to take money and impose labor on the poor.
translations.idiomatic: As the capital of Zhejiang Province, the county bore heavy corvée obligations; powerful families often colluded with crafty clerks to take bribes and shift labor onto the poor.

sentences.zh: 宗人令民自占甲乙，書於冊，以次簽役，役乃均。

translations.literal: Zongren ordered the people to declare their own ranks of priority, record them in a register, and draw lots for labor in order; thus the labor duties became equal.
translations.idiomatic: Zongren had citizens declare their own household standing, record it in a register, and draw lots for corvée in order until the burdens were fairly distributed.

sentences.zh: 嘗視事，有蛇升階，若有所訴。

translations.literal: Once while conducting business, a snake ascended the steps as if to lodge a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Once while holding court, a snake slithered up the steps as if pleading its case.

sentences.zh: 宗人曰：「爾有冤乎？

translations.literal: Zongren said: "Do you have a grievance?
translations.idiomatic: Zongren said: "Do you have a grievance?

sentences.zh: 吾為爾理。」

translations.literal: I will judge it for you."
translations.idiomatic: I will judge it for you."

sentences.zh: 蛇即出，遣隸尾之，入餅肆爐下。

translations.literal: The snake immediately went out; he sent a runner to follow it, and it entered under the oven of a cake shop.
