translations.idiomatic: The snake immediately departed; he sent a runner to follow it, and it entered beneath the oven of a cake shop.

sentences.zh: 發之，得僵屍，蓋肆主殺而瘞之也。

translations.literal: When they opened it up, they found a stiff corpse; it turned out the shopkeeper had killed someone and buried the body there.
translations.idiomatic: When they dug there, they found a corpse—the shopkeeper had murdered someone and buried the body beneath his oven.

sentences.zh: 又常行江中，有死人掛舟舵，推問，則裏無賴子所沉者。

translations.literal: Again, once traveling on the river, a dead man was caught on the boat's rudder; upon investigation, it turned out to be someone a local rogue had drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion while traveling on the river, a corpse snagged on his boat's rudder; investigation revealed it to be a victim drowned by a local ruffian.

sentences.zh: 遂俱伏法，邑民以為神。

translations.literal: Both were accordingly executed according to law; the county people regarded him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were executed, and the townspeople regarded him with awe.

sentences.zh: 按察使周新，廉介吏也，尤重宗人。

translations.literal: Regional inspector Zhou Xin was an incorrupt and upright official and especially valued Zongren.
translations.idiomatic: The regional inspector Zhou Xin was an incorrupt and upright official who held Zongren in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 一日，伺宗人出，潛入其室，見廚中惟銀魚臘一裹。

translations.literal: One day, waiting until Zongren went out, he secretly entered his room and saw in the kitchen only one packet of cured silver fish.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while Zongren was out, Zhou secretly entered his quarters and found in the kitchen only a single packet of cured silver fish.

sentences.zh: 新歎息，攜少許去。

translations.literal: Xin sighed and took a little and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sighed, took a small portion, and left.

sentences.zh: 明日召宗人共食，飲至醉，用儀仗導之歸。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned Zongren to dine together, drank until drunk, and had ceremonial escort guide him home.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he invited Zongren to dine, drank with him until drunk, and sent him home with ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 時呼為「錢塘一葉清」。

translations.literal: At the time he was called "Qiantang's one leaf of purity."
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was called "Qiantang's one leaf of purity."

sentences.zh: 十五年督工匠往營北京，卒于塗，新哭之累日。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he supervised craftsmen going to build Beijing and died on the road; Xin wept for him for many days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, while supervising craftsmen bound for the construction of Beijing, he died en route; Zhou Xin mourned him for days.

sentences.zh: 王源，字啟澤，龍岩人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan, courtesy name Qize, was a native of Longyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan, courtesy name Qize, was a native of Longyan.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年擢進士，授庶起士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he was selected as jinshi and appointed a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as jinshi in the second year of Yongle, he was appointed a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 改深澤知縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Shenze.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Shenze.

sentences.zh: 修學舍，築長堤，勸民及時嫁娶，革其爭財之俗。

translations.literal: He repaired school buildings, built long dikes, exhorted the people to marry in timely fashion, and reformed their custom of quarreling over property.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired school buildings, built long dikes, urged timely marriage, and reformed the custom of fighting over inheritances.

sentences.zh: 數上書論事，被詔征入都，又論時政得失，忤旨下吏。

translations.literal: Several times he submitted memorials discussing affairs; he was summoned by edict to the capital, again discussed the gains and losses of current policy, offended the imperial intent, and was handed over to the officials for trial.
translations.idiomatic: After repeatedly memorializing on state affairs, he was summoned to the capital, where his critique of current policy offended the throne and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 會赦復官，奏免逋負。

translations.literal: It happened that an amnesty restored him to office; he memorialized to remit overdue payments.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty restored him to office, and he memorialized to waive back taxes.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，輒發粟振救，坐是被逮。

translations.literal: In years of famine he invariably released grain for relief; on account of this he was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: During famine years he invariably distributed grain for relief and was arrested for it.

sentences.zh: 民爭先輸納，得贖還。

translations.literal: The people vied to pay taxes first and he was ransomed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The people competed to pay their taxes in advance, raising enough to ransom his release.

sentences.zh: 召為春坊司直郎，侍諸王講讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned as director of the Court of Dispatches in the Eastern Palace, attending the princes in lectures and study.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as director in the Eastern Palace, lecturing the princes.

sentences.zh: 遷衛府紀善，移松江同知，奏捐積逋數十萬石。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary of the Guard Prefecture, moved to vice-prefect of Songjiang, and memorialized to remit accumulated arrears of several hundred thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary of the Guard Prefecture, transferred to vice-prefect of Songjiang, and memorialized to cancel accumulated tax arrears of several hundred thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞歸養，服闋，除刑部郎中。

translations.literal: On account of his mother's age he begged to return and support her; when mourning was complete, he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to return home to care for his aged mother; after completing mourning, he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 英宗踐阼，擇廷臣十一人為知府，賜宴及敕，乘傳行。

translations.literal: When Yingzong ascended the throne, he selected eleven court officials as prefects, granted them a banquet and edicts, and sent them off by relay horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong ascended the throne, he selected eleven court officials to serve as prefects, granted them a banquet and imperial edicts, and dispatched them by relay post.

sentences.zh: 源得潮州府。

translations.literal: Yuan received Chaozhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was assigned Chaozhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城東有廣濟橋，歲久半圮壞，源斂民萬金重築之。

translations.literal: East of the city was the Guangji Bridge; after many years half had collapsed in ruin; Yuan collected ten thousand jin of gold from the people and rebuilt it heavily.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city stood the Guangji Bridge, half-ruined after long years; Yuan raised ten thousand jin in contributions and rebuilt it.

sentences.zh: 以其餘建亭，設先聖、四配、十哲像。

translations.literal: With the remainder he built a pavilion and installed images of the Sage, the Four Correlates, and the Ten Wise Ones.
translations.idiomatic: With the surplus funds he built a pavilion and installed images of Confucius, the Four Correlates, and the Ten Wise Ones.

sentences.zh: 刻《藍田呂氏鄉約》，擇民為約正、約副、約士，講肄其中，而時偕僚寀董率焉。

translations.literal: He had the "Community Compact of the Lü Family of Lantian" carved and printed, selected people as compact leader, deputy, and scholar, lectured and studied within it, and from time to time together with his colleagues supervised and led them.
translations.idiomatic: He had the Community Compact of the Lü Family of Lantian engraved and distributed, appointed community leaders and scholars, and held regular lectures there, himself joining his colleagues in supervising the effort.

sentences.zh: 西湖山上有大石為怪，源命鑿之，果獲石骷髏，怪遂息。

translations.literal: On West Lake Mountain was a great stone that behaved monstrously; Yuan ordered it drilled, and indeed obtained a stone skeleton; the monstrosity then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: A large stone on West Lake Mountain was said to be haunted; Yuan ordered it broken open, and a stone skeleton was found inside—the hauntings ceased.

sentences.zh: 乃琢為碑，大書「潮州知府王源除怪石」。

translations.literal: He then carved it into a stele and wrote in large characters: "Wang Yuan, Prefect of Chaozhou, removed the monstrous stone."
translations.idiomatic: He had it carved into a stele inscribed in large characters: "Wang Yuan, Prefect of Chaozhou, removed the haunted stone."

sentences.zh: 會杖一民死，民子訴諸朝，並以築橋建亭為源罪。

translations.literal: It happened that beating a commoner caused his death; the man's son appealed to the court, also citing the building of the bridge and pavilion as Yuan's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When a beating he administered killed a commoner, the victim's son appealed to the throne, also accusing Yuan of wrongdoing in building the bridge and pavilion.

sentences.zh: 逮至京，罪當贖徒。

translations.literal: Arrested and brought to the capital, the crime merited redeemable penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Brought to the capital as a prisoner, he was sentenced to redeemable penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 潮人相率叩閽，乃復其官。

translations.literal: The people of Chaozhou went in groups to knock on the palace gate, and he was then restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chaozhou petitioned en masse at the palace gates, and he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 久之，乞休。

translations.literal: After a long time, he begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, he petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 潮人奏留不獲，祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Chaozhou memorialized to keep him but did not succeed; they enshrined and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Chaozhou petitioned unsuccessfully to keep him, they built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 翟溥福，字本德，東莞人。

translations.literal: Zhai Pufu, courtesy name Bende, was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Pufu, courtesy name Bende, was a native of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 除青陽知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 九華虎為患，溥福檄山神，虎即殄。

translations.literal: Tigers on Jiuhua caused a scourge; Pufu issued a writ to the mountain god, and the tigers were immediately exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: When tigers on Mount Jiuhua terrorized the region, Pufu issued a proclamation to the mountain spirit—and the tigers vanished.

sentences.zh: 久之，移新淦，遷刑部主事，進員外郎，為尚書魏源所器。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Xingan, promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice, advanced to vice director, and was valued by Minister Wei Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Xingan, then promoted through the Ministry of Justice to vice director, where Minister Wei Yuan held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 正統元年七月詔舉廷臣堪為郡守者，源以溥福應，乃擢南康知府。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhengtong an edict summoned court officials fit to be prefects; Yuan recommended Pufu in response, and he was promoted to prefect of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhengtong, when the throne called for recommendations of court officials fit to serve as prefects, Wei Yuan nominated Pufu, who was appointed prefect of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 先是歲歉，民擅發富家粟，及收取漂流官木者，前守悉坐以盜，當死者百余人。

translations.literal: Previously, in a year of crop failure, the people on their own opened the grain stores of wealthy families, and those who collected drifting official timber—the previous prefect had charged them all as thieves, and more than a hundred deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during a famine year, people who had seized grain from wealthy stores or collected driftwood intended for official use had all been charged as thieves by the previous prefect—more than a hundred faced execution.

sentences.zh: 溥福閱實，杖而遣之。

translations.literal: Pufu reviewed the facts, beat them with the rod, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Pufu reviewed the cases, had the offenders beaten, and released them.

sentences.zh: 地濱鄱陽湖，舟遇風濤無所泊，為築石堤百餘丈，往來者便之。

translations.literal: The territory bordered Poyang Lake; boats encountering wind and waves had nowhere to moor; he built a stone dike of more than a hundred zhang, and those going back and forth found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Since the territory bordered Poyang Lake, where boats caught in storms had nowhere to anchor, he built a stone dike over a hundred zhang long, greatly easing travel.

sentences.zh: 廬山白鹿書院廢，溥福倡眾興復，延師訓其子弟，朔望躬詣講授。

translations.literal: The White Deer Grotto Academy on Mount Lu was abandoned; Pufu led the people in restoration, invited teachers to instruct their sons and younger brothers, and on the first and fifteenth of each month personally went to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the White Deer Grotto Academy on Mount Lu lay in ruins, Pufu led local restoration efforts, hired teachers for the community's youth, and personally lectured there on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 考績赴部，以年老乞歸。

translations.literal: At evaluation of performance he went to the ministry; on account of old age he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After his performance review in the capital, he petitioned to retire on account of his age.

sentences.zh: 侍郎趙新嘗撫江西，大聲曰：「翟君此邦第一賢守也，胡可聽其去。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhao Xin had once administered Jiangxi and said in a loud voice: "Master Zhai is this province's foremost virtuous prefect—how can we allow him to leave?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhao Xin, who had once administered Jiangxi, declared loudly: "Master Zhai is this province's foremost virtuous prefect—how can we allow him to leave?"

sentences.zh: 懇請累日，乃許之。

translations.literal: He earnestly petitioned for many days, and only then was it granted.
translations.idiomatic: After days of earnest petitioning, the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 辭郡之日，父老爭贐金帛，悉不受。

translations.literal: On the day he left the prefecture, the elders vied to present him with gold and silk; he entirely refused.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left office, elders competed to offer him parting gifts of gold and silk; he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 眾挽舟涕泣，因建詞湖堤祀之，又配享白鹿書院之三賢祠。

translations.literal: The people towed boats in tears; therefore they built a shrine on the lake dike to worship him, and also enshrined him in the Hall of Three Worthies at the White Deer Grotto Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The people wept as they towed his boat away; they then built a shrine on the lake dike in his honor and installed him in the Hall of Three Worthies at the White Deer Grotto Academy.

sentences.zh: 三賢者，唐李渤，宋周敦頤、硃熹也。

translations.literal: The three worthies were Li Bo of Tang, and Zhou Dunyi and Zhu Xi of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The three worthies were Li Bo of the Tang, and Zhou Dunyi and Zhu Xi of the Song.

sentences.zh: 李信圭，字君信，泰和人。

translations.literal: Li Xingui, styled Junxin, was a man of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingui, styled Junxin, was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 洪熙時舉賢良，授清河知縣。

translations.literal: During the Hongxi reign he was recommended as worthy and good, and was appointed magistrate of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongxi reign he was recommended as worthy and good, and appointed magistrate of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 縣瘠而沖，官艘日相銜，役夫動以千計。

translations.literal: The county was poor yet lay on a major thoroughfare; official boats lined up day after day, and corvée laborers often numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The county was impoverished yet lay on a major thoroughfare; official boats arrived in an unbroken stream, and corvée laborers often numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 前令請得沐陽五百人為助，然去家遠，艱於衣食。

translations.literal: The previous magistrate had requested five hundred men from Shuyang as helpers, but they lived far from home and found food and clothing hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The previous magistrate had obtained five hundred men from Shuyang as helpers, but they lived far from home and struggled to feed and clothe themselves.

sentences.zh: 信圭請免其助役，代輸清河浮征三之二，兩邑便之。

translations.literal: Xingui requested that their labor service be remitted and that two-thirds of Qinghe's transit levy be paid in their stead; both counties found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Xingui petitioned to exempt them from labor service and have Qinghe pay two-thirds of their transit levy instead—a arrangement that benefited both counties.

sentences.zh: 俗好發塚縱火，信圭設教戒十三條，令裏民書於牌，月朔望儆戒之。

translations.literal: The custom favored opening ancient tombs and setting fires; Xingui established thirteen admonitions, ordered the people of each ward to write them on placards, and on the first and fifteenth of each month warned them.
translations.idiomatic: The local custom favored grave-robbing and arson; Xingui issued thirteen admonitions, had each ward post them on placards, and on the first and fifteenth of every month read them as warnings.

sentences.zh: 且令書其民勤惰善惡以聞，俗為之變。

translations.literal: He also ordered that the diligence, idleness, good, and evil of the people be written down and reported, and the customs changed on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: He also required reports on each household's diligence, idleness, and conduct, and local customs changed as a result.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年上疏言：「本邑地廣人稀，地當沖要，使節絡繹，日發民挽舟。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande he submitted a memorial saying: "This county is broad in territory and sparse in population, yet lies on a vital route; envoys come in an unbroken stream, and the people are sent out daily to tow boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xuande he submitted a memorial stating: "Our county is vast yet sparsely populated, and lies on a vital route; envoys arrive in an unbroken stream, and the people are drafted daily to tow boats.

sentences.zh: 丁壯既盡，役及老稚，妨廢農桑。

translations.literal: Once the able-bodied were exhausted, service extended to the old and young, obstructing and ruining farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Once the able-bodied were exhausted, the corvée extended to the old and young, leaving farming and sericulture in ruins.

sentences.zh: 前年兵部有令，公事亟者舟予五人，緩者則否。

translations.literal: The year before last the Ministry of War had issued an order: for urgent official business each boat was to be given five men; for non-urgent business, not.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, the Ministry of War had ordered that urgent official boats receive five towmen each, while non-urgent ones receive none.

sentences.zh: 今此令不行，役夫無限，有一舟至四五十人者。

translations.literal: Now this order is not enforced; laborers are unlimited, and for one boat there are sometimes as many as forty or fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: That order is no longer enforced; laborers are assigned without limit, and a single boat sometimes takes forty or fifty men.

sentences.zh: 凶威所加，誰敢詰問。

translations.literal: Where brutal authority is applied, who dares to question it?
translations.idiomatic: Under such brutal authority, who would dare to protest?

sentences.zh: 或遇快風，步追不及，則官舫人役沒其所齎衣糧，俾受寒餒。

translations.literal: Sometimes when a strong wind arose, those on foot could not keep up; then the men on the official barge would seize the clothing and provisions they carried, leaving them to suffer cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: When a strong wind arose, towmen on foot could not keep pace; officials on the barges would then seize their clothing and provisions, leaving them to suffer cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 乞申明前令，哀此憚人。」

translations.literal: I beg that the former order be clarified and enforced, and that pity be shown for these people who live in dread."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the earlier order be clarified and enforced, and that pity be shown for these people who live in dread."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 八年春，又言：「自江、淮達京師，沿河郡縣悉令軍民挽舟，若無衛軍則民夫盡出有司，州縣歲發二三千人，晝夜以俟。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he again said: "From the Yangtze and Huai to the capital, every county and prefecture along the river is ordered to have soldiers and civilians tow boats; if there are no garrison troops, then all civilian laborers are supplied by the local offices; prefectures and counties dispatch two or three thousand men each year, waiting day and night.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he submitted another memorial: "From the Yangtze and Huai to the capital, every county along the river drafts soldiers and civilians to tow boats; where no garrison troops are available, local offices supply all the laborers—prefectures and counties dispatch two or three thousand men each year, kept waiting day and night.

sentences.zh: 而上官又不分別雜泛差役，一體派及。

translations.literal: Yet superior officials also fail to distinguish miscellaneous and general corvée duties, and assign them all alike.
translations.idiomatic: Yet superior officials make no distinction among miscellaneous corvée duties and assign them all indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 致土田荒蕪，民無蓄積。

translations.literal: This has caused fields to lie waste and the people to have no stores.
translations.idiomatic: Fields lie fallow and the people have no reserves.

sentences.zh: 稍遇歉歲，輒老稚相攜，緣道乞食，實可憫傷。

translations.literal: Whenever a lean year comes, the old and young go off together, begging along the roads—a sight truly pitiable and grievous.
translations.idiomatic: In even a slightly bad year, the old and young set out together to beg along the roads—a sight truly pitiable.

sentences.zh: 請自儀真抵通州，盡免其雜徭，俾得盡力農田，兼供夫役。」

translations.literal: I request that from Yizhen to Tongzhou all miscellaneous corvée be entirely remitted, so that the people may devote themselves fully to farming while also supplying labor service."
translations.idiomatic: I request that from Yizhen to Tongzhou all miscellaneous corvée be remitted, so the people may devote themselves to farming while still supplying tow labor."

sentences.zh: 帝亦從之。

translations.literal: The emperor also granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted this as well.

sentences.zh: 自是，他郡亦蒙其澤。

translations.literal: From this time on, other prefectures also shared in the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, other prefectures benefited as well.

sentences.zh: 自明興至洪、宣、正統間，民淳俗富，吏易為治。

translations.literal: From the founding of the Ming through the Hongxi, Xuande, and Zhengtong reigns, the people were simple and customs prosperous, and officials found governance easy.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the Ming through the Hongxi, Xuande, and Zhengtong reigns, the people were upright, customs were prosperous, and officials found governance easy.

sentences.zh: 而其時長吏亦多勵長者行，以循良見稱。

translations.literal: At that time senior officials also often encouraged conduct befitting elders and were praised as virtuous administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials of that era often encouraged upright conduct and won renown as virtuous administrators.

sentences.zh: 其秩滿奏留者，不可勝紀，略舉數人列於篇。

translations.literal: Those whose terms expired and who were memorialized to be retained cannot be fully recorded; a few are briefly listed in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Those retained at the end of their terms are too numerous to record in full; a few are listed here by way of example.

sentences.zh: 孫浩，永樂中知邵陽，遭喪去官。

translations.literal: Sun Hao served as magistrate of Shaoyang during the Yongle reign and left office upon a bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao served as magistrate of Shaoyang during the Yongle reign and left office to mourn a parent's death.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，陝西按察使頌浩前政，請令補威寧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, the Shaanxi surveillance commissioner praised Hao's earlier administration and requested that he be appointed to Weining.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi, the Shaanxi surveillance commissioner praised Hao's earlier administration and requested his appointment to Weining.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉歎，即命起復。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor commended and sighed with approval, and immediately ordered his recall from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande Emperor expressed warm approval and immediately ordered him recalled from mourning.

sentences.zh: 久之，超擢辰州知府。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted beyond the ordinary to prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted directly to prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 薛慎知長清，以親喪去。

translations.literal: Xue Shen served as magistrate of Changqing and left on account of a parent's death.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shen served as magistrate of Changqing and left office to mourn a parent's death.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，長清民知慎服闋，相率詣京師乞再任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, when the people of Changqing learned that Shen's mourning period had ended, they went together to the capital to beg that he serve again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi, when the people of Changqing learned that Shen's mourning period had ended, they went together to the capital to petition for his return.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書蹇義以聞，言長清別除知縣已久，即如民言，又當更易。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Jian Yi reported this, saying that Changqing had long since received another appointed magistrate; even if the people's request were granted, there would again have to be a change.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Jian Yi reported this, noting that Changqing had long had another appointed magistrate; even if the people's request were granted, another replacement would be required.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「國家置守令，但欲其得民心，苟民心不得，雖屢易何害。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The state appoints prefects and magistrates only to win the people's hearts; if the people's hearts are not won, what harm is there in changing them repeatedly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The state appoints prefects and magistrates only to win the people's hearts; if the people's hearts are not won, what harm is there in changing them repeatedly?"

sentences.zh: 遂還之。

translations.literal: He was then restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was then restored to office.

sentences.zh: 吳原知吳橋，洪熙中，九載考績赴部。

translations.literal: Wu Yuan served as magistrate of Wuqiao; during Hongxi, at the nine-year performance review he went to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuan served as magistrate of Wuqiao; during the Hongxi reign, at his nine-year performance review he traveled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 縣民詣闕乞留，帝從之。

translations.literal: The county people went to the palace gate to beg that he be retained, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: County residents petitioned at the palace gate for his retention, and the emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 暢宣知泰安，以母憂去。

translations.literal: Chang Xuan served as magistrate of Tai'an and left on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xuan served as magistrate of Tai'an and left office to mourn his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 民頌于副使鄺埜，以聞，仁宗命服闋還任。

translations.literal: The people praised him to Vice Commissioner Kuang Ye, who reported it; the Renzong Emperor ordered that when his mourning ended he return to office.
translations.idiomatic: The people praised him to Vice Commissioner Kuang Ye, who reported it; the Renzong Emperor ordered that he return to office when his mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 宣德改元，宣服闋，吏部以請。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Xuande, Xuan's mourning ended, and the Ministry of Personnel submitted the request.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande reign began, Xuan's mourning period ended, and the Ministry of Personnel submitted the request for his return.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「民欲之，監司言之，固當從，況有先帝之命乎。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The people want this, and the supervising officials have spoken for it—it should certainly be granted, especially since there was the former emperor's command."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The people want this, and the supervising officials have spoken for it—it should certainly be granted, especially since the former emperor already ordered it."

sentences.zh: 遂如其請。

translations.literal: His request was then granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 劉伯吉知碭山，以親喪去。

translations.literal: Liu Boji served as magistrate of Dangshan and left on account of a parent's death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Boji served as magistrate of Dangshan and left office to mourn a parent's death.

sentences.zh: 服除，碭山民守闕下，求再任。

translations.literal: When his mourning ended, the people of Dangshan waited below the palace gate, seeking his reappointment.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, the people of Dangshan waited at the palace gate, petitioning for his reappointment.

sentences.zh: 吏部言新令已在碭山二年矣。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel said that the new magistrate had already been in Dangshan for two years.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel noted that the new magistrate had already served in Dangshan for two years.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「新者勝舊，則民不復思。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If the new man surpasses the old, the people will not again think of the old one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If the new magistrate surpasses the old, the people will not still long for the old one.

sentences.zh: 今久而又思，其賢于新者可知矣。」

translations.literal: Now after so long they still think of him—the fact that he surpasses the new man can be known."
translations.idiomatic: Yet after so long they still long for him—clear proof that he surpasses the new man."

sentences.zh: 遂易之。

translations.literal: He was then restored in place of the other.
translations.idiomatic: Boji was then restored in the new magistrate's place.

sentences.zh: 孔公朝，永樂時知甯陽，坐與同僚飲酒忿爭，並遣戍。

translations.literal: Kong Gongchao served as magistrate of Ningyang during the Yongle reign; he was sentenced for drinking and quarreling angrily with a colleague, and both were sent to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Gongchao served as magistrate of Ningyang during the Yongle reign; after drinking and quarreling with a colleague, both men were sentenced to frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 部民屢叩閽乞還，皆不許。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture repeatedly knocked at the palace gate to beg his return, but each time it was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The people repeatedly petitioned at the palace gate for his return, but each request was denied.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年詔求賢，有以公朝薦者，甯陽人聞之，又相率叩閽乞公朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande an edict sought the worthy; someone recommended Gongchao; when the people of Ningyang heard of it, they again went together to knock at the palace gate to beg for Gongchao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande an edict sought worthy men; when someone recommended Gongchao, the people of Ningyang heard of it and again petitioned at the palace gate for his return.

sentences.zh: 帝顧尚書蹇義曰：「公朝去甯陽已二十餘載，民奏乞不已，此非良吏耶？

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Minister Jian Yi and said: "Gongchao has been away from Ningyang for more than twenty years, yet the people petition without cease—is this not a good official?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Minister Jian Yi and said: "Gongchao has been away from Ningyang for more than twenty years, yet the people never cease petitioning for him—is this not proof of a good official?

sentences.zh: 可即與之。」

translations.literal: He may be given the post at once."
translations.idiomatic: Restore him at once."

sentences.zh: 郭完知會寧，為奸人所訐被逮。

translations.literal: Guo Wan served as magistrate of Huining and was arrested after being denounced by a malicious person.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wan served as magistrate of Huining and was arrested after a malicious accuser denounced him.

sentences.zh: 裏老伏闕訟冤乞還，帝亦許之。

translations.literal: Elders of the wards prostrated themselves at the palace gate to plead his innocence and beg his return, and the emperor also granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Elders of the community prostrated themselves at the palace gate to plead his innocence and petition for his return, and the emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 徐士宗知貴溪，宣德六年三考俱最。

translations.literal: Xu Shizong served as magistrate of Guixi; in the sixth year of Xuande all three performance reviews were rated highest.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shizong served as magistrate of Guixi; in the sixth year of Xuande he received the highest rating in all three performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 民詣闕乞留，詔增二秩還任。

translations.literal: The people went to the palace gate to beg that he be retained; an edict raised him two ranks and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned at the palace gate for his retention; an edict promoted him two ranks and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 郭南知常熟，正統十二年以老致仕。

translations.literal: Guo Nan served as magistrate of Changshu; in the twelfth year of Zhengtong he retired on account of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nan served as magistrate of Changshu; in the twelfth year of Zhengtong he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 父老乞還任，英宗許之。

translations.literal: The elders begged that he return to office, and the Yingzong Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Local elders petitioned for his return, and the Yingzong Emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 張璟知平山，秩滿，士民乞留，英宗命進秩復任。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing served as magistrate of Pingshan; when his term expired, gentry and commoners begged that he be retained, and the Yingzong Emperor ordered his promotion in rank and return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing served as magistrate of Pingshan; when his term expired, gentry and commoners petitioned for his retention, and the Yingzong Emperor promoted him and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，母憂去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign he left on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign he left office to mourn his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 復從士民請，奪情視事。

translations.literal: Again acceding to the gentry and commoners' request, he was dispensed from mourning and resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: Again acceding to the people's petition, he was dispensed from mourning and resumed office.

sentences.zh: 徐榮知槁城，親喪去官。

translations.literal: Xu Rong served as magistrate of Gaocheng and left office upon a parent's death.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rong served as magistrate of Gaocheng and left office to mourn a parent's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，部民乞罷新令而還榮，英宗如其請。

translations.literal: When his mourning ended, the people of the prefecture begged that the new magistrate be dismissed and Rong restored; the Yingzong Emperor granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, the people petitioned to dismiss the new magistrate and restore Rong; the Yingzong Emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，秩滿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign his term expired.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign his term expired.

sentences.zh: 復徇民請，留之。

translations.literal: Again yielding to the people's request, he was retained.
translations.idiomatic: Again acceding to the people's petition, he was retained.

sentences.zh: 何澄知安福，被劾。

translations.literal: He Cheng served as magistrate of Anfu and was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: He Cheng served as magistrate of Anfu and was impeached.

sentences.zh: 民詣闕乞留，英宗命還任。

translations.literal: The people went to the palace gate to beg that he be retained, and the Yingzong Emperor ordered his return to office.
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned at the palace gate for his retention, and the Yingzong Emperor ordered his return to office.

sentences.zh: 乃築寅陂，浚管道，復密湖之舊，大興水利。

translations.literal: He then built the Yin Embankment, dredged irrigation channels, restored the former condition of Mihu Lake, and greatly developed water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: He then built the Yin Embankment, dredged irrigation channels, restored Mihu Lake to its former condition, and undertook major waterworks.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當遷，侍講劉球為民代請，帝復留之。

translations.literal: When his term expired and he was due for transfer, Reader-in-waiting Liu Qiu petitioned on the people's behalf, and the emperor again retained him.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired and he was due for promotion, Reader-in-waiting Liu Qiu petitioned on the people's behalf, and the emperor retained him again.

sentences.zh: 田玉知桐鄉，丁艱去。

translations.literal: Tian Yu served as magistrate of Tongxiang and left upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yu served as magistrate of Tongxiang and left office to mourn his father's death.

sentences.zh: 英宗以部民及巡撫周忱請，還其任。

translations.literal: The Yingzong Emperor, on the petition of the prefecture's people and Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen, restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: At the petition of local residents and Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen, the Yingzong Emperor restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 其他若內丘馬旭、桐廬楊信、北流李禧、洋縣王黼、保安張庸、獲鹿吳韞、扶風宋端，皆當宣宗之世，以九載奏最。

translations.literal: Others such as Ma Xu of Neiqiu, Yang Xin of Tonglu, Li Xi of Beiliu, Wang Fu of Yang County, Zhang Yong of Bao'an, Wu Yun of Huolu, and Song Duan of Fufeng—all during the Xuande Emperor's reign, at the nine-year review submitted the highest rating.
translations.idiomatic: Others—Ma Xu of Neiqiu, Yang Xin of Tonglu, Li Xi of Beiliu, Wang Fu of Yang County, Zhang Yong of Bao'an, Wu Yun of Huolu, and Song Duan of Fufeng—all received the highest rating at their nine-year review during the Xuande reign.

sentences.zh: 為民乞留，即加秩留任者也。

translations.literal: When the people begged that they be retained, they were immediately promoted in rank and kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: When the people petitioned for their retention, they were promoted and kept in office.

sentences.zh: 時帝方重循良，而吏部尚書蹇義尤慎擇守令，考察明恕。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor greatly valued virtuous administrators, and Minister of Personnel Jian Yi was especially careful in selecting prefects and magistrates, examining them with clarity and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor greatly valued virtuous administrators, and Minister of Personnel Jian Yi was especially careful in selecting prefects and magistrates and reviewing them with clarity and leniency.

sentences.zh: 沿及英宗，吏治淳厚，部民奏留率報可。

translations.literal: This continued into the Yingzong reign; official governance was pure and generous, and petitions from prefecture peoples for retention were generally approved.
translations.idiomatic: This continued into the Yingzong reign; governance was upright and generous, and petitions for officials' retention were generally approved.

sentences.zh: 然其間亦有作奸者。

translations.literal: Yet among them there were also those who committed fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Yet there were also frauds among them.

sentences.zh: 永甯稅課大使劉迪刲羊置酒，邀耆老請留。

translations.literal: Liu Di, tax-assessment commissioner of Yongning, slaughtered a sheep and set out wine, inviting elders to petition for his retention.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Di, tax commissioner of Yongning, slaughtered a sheep and hosted a feast, inviting elders to petition for his retention.

sentences.zh: 宣宗怒，下之吏。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor was angry and handed him over to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande Emperor was enraged and handed him over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 漢中同知王聚亦張宴求屬吏保奏為知府。

translations.literal: Wang Ju, vice prefect of Hanzhong, also held a banquet and sought subordinate officials' guarantee-memorials for appointment as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju, vice prefect of Hanzhong, also held a banquet and solicited guarantee-memorials from subordinates for promotion to prefect.

sentences.zh: 事聞，宣宗並屬吏罪之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Xuande Emperor punished both him and the subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, the Xuande Emperor punished both Wang Ju and the subordinate officials who had signed.

sentences.zh: 自後，部民奏留，率下所司核實雲。

translations.literal: From then on, when prefecture peoples petitioned for retention, the cases were generally sent down to the responsible offices for verification.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, petitions for officials' retention were generally referred to the responsible offices for verification.

sentences.zh: 張宗璉，字重器，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zonglian, styled Zhongqi, was a man of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zonglian, styled Zhongqi, was a native of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 改庶起士，授刑部主事，錄囚廣東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to junior compiler, appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, and sent to review prisoners in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a junior compiler, then principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, and sent to review prisoners in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，擢左中允。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor ascended the throne, he was promoted to Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor ascended the throne, he was promoted to Left Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 會詔朝臣舉所知，禮部郎中況鐘以宗璉名上。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered court officials to recommend those they knew; Bureau Director Kuang Zhong of the Ministry of Rites submitted Zonglian's name.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered court officials to recommend men of talent, Bureau Director Kuang Zhong of the Ministry of Rites submitted Zonglian's name.

sentences.zh: 帝問少傅楊士奇曰：「人皆舉外吏，鐘舉京官，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Junior Tutor Yang Shiqi: "Everyone recommends outside officials; Zhong recommends a capital official—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Junior Tutor Yang Shiqi: "Everyone else recommends local officials; why does Zhong recommend a capital official?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「宗璉賢，臣與侍讀學士王直將舉之，不意為鐘所先耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Zonglian is worthy; I and Reader-in-waiting Wang Zhi were about to recommend him—I did not expect Zhong to get there first."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Zonglian is worthy; Reader-in-waiting Wang Zhi and I were about to recommend him—we did not expect Zhong to get there first."

sentences.zh: 帝喜，曰：「鐘能知宗璉，亦賢矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "If Zhong could recognize Zonglian's worth, he too is worthy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said: "If Zhong could recognize Zonglian's worth, he too is worthy."

sentences.zh: 由是知鐘，而擢宗璉南京大理丞。

translations.literal: From this he came to know Zhong, and promoted Zonglian to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: From this he came to know Zhong, and promoted Zonglian to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，詔遣吏部侍郎黃宗載等十五人出厘各省軍籍，宗璉往福建。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande an edict dispatched Vice Minister Huang Zongzai and fourteen others to rectify military registers in each province; Zonglian went to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande an edict dispatched Vice Minister Huang Zongzai and fourteen others to rectify military registers in the provinces; Zonglian was sent to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 明年坐奏事忤旨，謫常州同知。

translations.literal: The next year, on account of a memorial that displeased the throne, he was demoted to vice prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after a memorial displeased the throne, he was demoted to vice prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝遣御史李立理江南軍籍，檄宗璉自隨。

translations.literal: The court dispatched Censor Li Li to settle military registers in Jiangnan and ordered Zonglian to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Censor Li Li to settle military registers in Jiangnan and ordered Zonglian to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 立受黠軍詞，多逮平民實伍，宗璉數爭之。

translations.literal: Li accepted the testimony of cunning soldiers and often seized commoners to fill out military rolls; Zonglian repeatedly disputed this.
translations.idiomatic: Li accepted the testimony of cunning soldiers and often seized commoners to fill military rolls; Zonglian repeatedly protested.

sentences.zh: 立怒，宗璉輒臥地乞杖，曰「請代百姓死」，免株累甚眾。

translations.literal: Li grew angry; Zonglian would then lie on the ground begging to be beaten, saying "I ask to die in the common people's place," and thus spared very many from being implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Li grew furious; Zonglian would lie on the ground begging to be beaten, crying "Let me die in the people's place"—and thus spared many from being implicated.

sentences.zh: 初，宗璉使廣東，務廉恕。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zonglian served in Guangdong, he devoted himself to integrity and leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during his service in Guangdong, Zonglian had devoted himself to integrity and leniency.

sentences.zh: 至是見立暴橫，心積不平，疽廢背卒。

translations.literal: Now, seeing Li's brutal arrogance, his heart accumulated resentment; an ulcer on his back disabled him and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Now, witnessing Li's brutal arrogance, resentment built in his heart until a festering ulcer on his back disabled him and he died.

sentences.zh: 常州民白衣送喪者千餘人，為建祠君山。

translations.literal: More than a thousand people of Changzhou in white mourning clothes escorted his funeral procession, and a shrine was built for him on Jun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand Changzhou residents in white mourning escorted his funeral procession, and a shrine was built in his honor on Jun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 宗璉蒞郡，不攜妻子，病亟召醫，室無燈燭。

translations.literal: When Zonglian arrived to take up his prefectural post, he did not bring wife and children; when seriously ill he summoned a doctor—his room had no lamp or candle.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonglian took up his prefectural post, he came without his wife and children. When he fell gravely ill and summoned a doctor, his room had no lamp or candle.

sentences.zh: 童子從外索取油一盂入，宗璉立卻之，其清峻如此。

translations.literal: A page boy went outside and fetched a bowl of oil and brought it in; Zonglian immediately refused it—such was his pure austerity.
translations.idiomatic: A page boy went out and brought back a bowl of oil; Zonglian immediately refused it—such was his austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 李驥，字尚德，郯城人。

translations.literal: Li Ji, styled Shangde, was a man of Tancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, styled Shangde, was a native of Tancheng.

sentences.zh: 舉洪武二十六年鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu (1393).

sentences.zh: 入國學，居三年，授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy, stayed three years, and was appointed supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy, studied there three years, and was appointed supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時關市譏商旅，發及囊篋，驥奏止之。

translations.literal: At the time customs posts inspected traveling merchants, searching even bags and cases; Ji memorialized to stop this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time customs posts inspected traveling merchants and searched even their bags and cases; Ji memorialized to halt the practice.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 建文時，薦起新鄉知縣，招流亡，給以農具，復業者數千人。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he was recommended and reinstated as magistrate of Xinxiang; he recruited refugees, supplied them with farm tools, and several thousand returned to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign he was recommended and reinstated as magistrate of Xinxiang. He gathered refugees, supplied them with farm tools, and several thousand people returned to productive work.

sentences.zh: 內艱去官，民相率奏留者數四，不許。

translations.literal: When mourning his mother he left office; the people repeatedly petitioned in groups to keep him—four times—but permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office to mourn his mother, the people petitioned in groups four times to keep him, but each request was denied.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，服闋，改知東安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, when his mourning period ended, he was reassigned as magistrate of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongle reign, when his mourning period ended, he was reassigned as magistrate of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 事有病民，輒奏於朝，罷免之。

translations.literal: Whenever matters harmed the people, he memorialized the court and had the officials removed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he found policies that harmed the people, he memorialized the court and had the responsible officials dismissed.

sentences.zh: 有嫠婦子齧死，訴於驥。

translations.literal: A widow's child was bitten to death; she appealed to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: A widow whose child had been killed by a bite came to appeal to Ji.

sentences.zh: 驥禱城隍神，深自咎責。

translations.literal: Ji prayed to the City God and deeply blamed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ji prayed to the City God and blamed himself deeply.

sentences.zh: 明旦，狼死於其所。

translations.literal: The next morning the wolf died at that place.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the wolf was found dead at the spot.

sentences.zh: 侍郎李昶等交薦，擢刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Chang and others jointly recommended him, and he was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Chang and others jointly recommended him, and he was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 奏陳十餘事，多見採納。

translations.literal: He memorialized more than ten matters; many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized more than ten proposals, many of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 坐累，謫役保安。

translations.literal: On account of being implicated, he was banished to serve at Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: After being implicated in another's offense, he was banished to serve at Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 洪熙時，有詔求賢，薦為御史。

translations.literal: During Hongxi, an edict sought worthy men and he was recommended as censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongxi reign, when an edict sought worthy men, he was recommended and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 陳經國利民十事，仁宗嘉納。

translations.literal: He set forth ten measures to govern the state and benefit the people; Renzong praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He presented ten measures for governing the state and benefiting the people, and Renzong praised and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年巡視倉場，軍高祥盜倉粟，驥執而鞫之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande, while inspecting granaries, soldier Gao Xiang stole granary grain; Ji seized and interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xuande (1430), while inspecting granaries, he found that soldier Gao Xiang had stolen granary grain; Ji seized and interrogated him.

sentences.zh: 祥父妾言，祥與張貴等同盜，驥受貴等賄故獨罪祥。

translations.literal: Gao Xiang's father's concubine said Xiang stole together with Zhang Gui and others, but Ji had accepted bribes from Gui and the others and therefore blamed Xiang alone.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiang's father's concubine claimed that Xiang had stolen together with Zhang Gui and others, but that Ji had taken bribes from Gui and the others and therefore punished Xiang alone.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎施禮遂論驥死。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Shi Li of the Ministry of Justice then sentenced Ji to death.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Shi Li of the Ministry of Justice then sentenced Ji to death.

sentences.zh: 驥上章自辨，帝曰：「御史即擒盜，安肯納賄！」

translations.literal: Ji submitted a memorial in his own defense; the emperor said: "A censor who just caught a thief—how could he accept bribes!"
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted a memorial defending himself. The emperor said: "A censor who has just caught a thief—how could he accept bribes!"

sentences.zh: 命偕都察院再訊，驥果枉。

translations.literal: He ordered a re-investigation jointly with the Censorate; Ji was indeed wronged.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a joint reinvestigation with the Censorate, and Ji was indeed found to have been wronged.

sentences.zh: 帝乃切責禮，而復驥官。

translations.literal: The emperor then sternly rebuked Shi Li and restored Ji's office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sternly rebuked Shi Li and restored Ji to office.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，擇廷臣二十五人為郡守，奉敕以行。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month, twenty-five court officials were selected as prefects and dispatched under imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: That November, twenty-five court officials were selected as prefects and sent out under imperial command.

sentences.zh: 驥授河南知府，肇慶則給事中王瑩〗，瓊州則戶部郎中徐鑒，汀州則禮部員外郎許敬軒，寧波則刑部主事鄭珞，撫州則大理寺正王升，後皆以政績著。

translations.literal: Ji was appointed prefect of Henan; for Zhaoqing it was supervising secretary Wang Ying; for Qiongzhou, bureau director Xu Jian of the Ministry of Revenue; for Tingzhou, vice director Xu Jingxuan of the Ministry of Rites; for Ningbo, secretary Zheng Luo of the Ministry of Justice; for Fuzhou, chief of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Sheng—all later became known for their administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was appointed prefect of Henan; Wang Ying, a supervising secretary, was sent to Zhaoqing; Xu Jian, a bureau director of the Ministry of Revenue, to Qiongzhou; Xu Jingxuan, a vice director of the Ministry of Rites, to Tingzhou; Zheng Luo, a secretary of the Ministry of Justice, to Ningbo; and Wang Sheng, chief of the Court of Judicial Review, to Fuzhou—all later became noted for their achievements in office.

sentences.zh: 河南境多盜，驥為設火甲，一戶被盜，一甲償之。

translations.literal: Henan had many bandits; Ji instituted the fire-ward system—if one household was robbed, the whole ward compensated the loss.
translations.idiomatic: Henan had many bandits, so Ji instituted a mutual-security ward system: if one household was robbed, the entire ward made restitution.

sentences.zh: 犯者，大署其門曰盜賊之家。

translations.literal: Offenders had posted on their doors in large characters: "House of Thieves."
translations.idiomatic: Offenders had the words "House of Thieves" posted in large characters on their doors.

sentences.zh: 又為《勸教文》，振木鐸以徇之。

translations.literal: He also composed an "Essay on Encouraging Education" and had it proclaimed with the wooden clapper.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an "Essay on Encouraging Education" and had it proclaimed throughout the prefecture with a wooden clapper.

sentences.zh: 自是人鹹改行，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: From then on people all reformed their conduct, and things lost on the road were not picked up.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the people reformed their conduct, and lost property was left untouched on the roads.

sentences.zh: 郡有伊王府，王數請囑，不從。

translations.literal: The prefecture had the Yi princely establishment; the prince repeatedly asked for favors, but Ji would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture housed the Yi princely establishment; the prince repeatedly asked for special favors, but Ji refused.

sentences.zh: 中官及校卒虐民，又為驥所抑，恨甚。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and guard soldiers abused the people and were likewise restrained by Ji; they hated him intensely.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and guard soldiers who abused the people were likewise restrained by Ji, and they hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及冬至，令驥以四更往陪位行禮。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice they ordered Ji to come at the fourth watch to accompany them in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice they ordered Ji to come at the fourth watch to take part in the ceremonial observances.

sentences.zh: 及驥如期往，誣驥後期，執而桎梏之，次日乃釋。

translations.literal: When Ji arrived on time, they falsely claimed he was late, seized him and put him in shackles, and only released him the next day.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji arrived on schedule, they falsely accused him of being late, seized him, put him in shackles, and did not release him until the next day.

sentences.zh: 驥奏聞，帝怒，貽書讓王，府中承奉、長史、典儀悉逮置於理。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized the throne; the emperor was angry, sent a letter rebuking the prince, and had all the establishment's attendants, chief instructor, and ceremonial officers arrested and turned over for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Ji reported the matter to the throne. The emperor was furious, sent a letter rebuking the prince, and had all the princely establishment's attendants, chief instructor, and ceremonial officers arrested and turned over for trial.

sentences.zh: 驥持身端恪，晏居雖幾席必正。

translations.literal: Ji maintained himself with upright integrity; even at leisure his mat and seat were always properly arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Ji conducted himself with upright integrity; even in private his mat and seat were always properly arranged.

sentences.zh: 蒞郡六年卒，年七十。

translations.literal: After six years as prefect he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: After six years as prefect he died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 士民赴吊，鹹哭失聲。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners came to mourn; all wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners came to mourn him, weeping aloud.

sentences.zh: 王瑩，鄞人，起家舉人。

translations.literal: Wang Ying, a man of Yin, entered official life as a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying, a native of Yin, entered official service as a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 居肇慶九年，進秩二等，後徙知西安。

translations.literal: He served at Zhaoqing nine years, was promoted two ranks, and later was transferred as magistrate of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Zhaoqing for nine years, was promoted two ranks, and was later transferred to serve as magistrate of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 徐鑒，宜興人。

translations.literal: Xu Jian, a man of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 在瓊四年卒，郡人祀之九賢祠。

translations.literal: He served at Qiong four years and died; the people of the prefecture enshrined him in the Hall of Nine Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Qiongzhou for four years and died; the people of the prefecture enshrined him in the Hall of Nine Worthies.

sentences.zh: 許敬軒，天臺人。

translations.literal: Xu Jingxuan, a man of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingxuan was a native of Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 起家國子生。

translations.literal: He entered official life as an Imperial Academy student.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official service as an Imperial Academy student.

sentences.zh: 守汀特糾參政陳羽貪暴，宣宗為逮治羽。

translations.literal: As prefect of Ting he specifically impeached Vice Commissioner Chen Yu for greed and cruelty; the Xuanzong had Yu arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Tingzhou he impeached Vice Commissioner Chen Yu for greed and cruelty, and the Xuanzong had Yu arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 卒官，士民爭賻之。

translations.literal: He died in office; officials and commoners competed to contribute funeral offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, and officials and commoners vied to contribute to his funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 鄭珞，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Zheng Luo, a man of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luo was a native of Min County.

sentences.zh: 起家進士。

translations.literal: He entered official life as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official service as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 守寧波，以艱去。

translations.literal: As prefect of Ningbo, he left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as prefect of Ningbo, he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 會海寇入犯，民數千詣闕乞留，詔奪情復任。

translations.literal: When sea bandits invaded, several thousand people went to the capital to beg that he be kept; an edict set aside mourning and restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: When sea bandits invaded, several thousand people went to the capital to petition for his retention; an edict exempted him from mourning obligations and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 嘗劾中使呂可烈無狀，帝為誅可烈。

translations.literal: He once impeached eunuch envoy Lü Kēliè for misconduct; the emperor had Kēliè executed for it.
translations.idiomatic: He once impeached the eunuch envoy Lü Kēliè for misconduct, and the emperor had Kēliè executed.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢浙江參政。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to vice commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to vice commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 王升，龍溪人。

translations.literal: Wang Sheng, a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sheng was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 起家進士。

translations.literal: He entered official life as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official service as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 在郡九載，以部民乞留，增秩還任。

translations.literal: He served at the prefecture nine years; because the people of his district petitioned to keep him, his rank was raised and he returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: He served at the prefecture for nine years; when the people of his district petitioned to keep him, his rank was raised and he returned to office.

sentences.zh: 以疾歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 李湘，字永懷，泰和人。

translations.literal: Li Xiang, styled Yonghuai, was a man of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang, styled Yonghuai, was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，由國子生理刑都察院。

translations.literal: During Yongle, from an Imperial Academy student he served in the Court of Judicial Review under the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, after serving as an Imperial Academy student, he worked in the Court of Judicial Review under the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 以才擢東平知州，常祿外一無所取，訓誡吏民若家人然。

translations.literal: For his talent he was promoted to magistrate of Dongping; aside from his regular salary he took nothing at all, and admonished officials and people like members of his own family.
translations.idiomatic: For his talent he was promoted to magistrate of Dongping. Aside from his regular salary he took nothing, and he admonished officials and commoners as if they were members of his own family.

sentences.zh: 城東有大村壩，源出岱嶽，雨潦輒為民患，奏發丁夫堤之。

translations.literal: East of the city was the Great Village Dam, whose source came from Mount Tai; when rains flooded it frequently harmed the people; he memorialized to dispatch corvée laborers to dike it.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city was the Great Village Dam, whose waters came from Mount Tai; flooding after heavy rains often harmed the people, so he memorialized to dispatch corvée laborers to build dikes.

sentences.zh: 州及所轄五邑，地多荒蕪，力督民墾辟，公私皆實。

translations.literal: The prefecture and its five subordinate counties had much wasteland; he vigorously supervised the people in opening new fields, and both public and private stores were filled.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and its five subordinate counties had much wasteland; he vigorously supervised the people in clearing and cultivating it until both public and private stores were well filled.

sentences.zh: 會舊官還任，將解去。

translations.literal: When the former official returned to his post, he was about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: When the former official returned to his post, Xiang was about to leave office.

sentences.zh: 民群乞於朝，帝從其請。

translations.literal: The people petitioned the court in groups; the emperor granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned the court in groups, and the emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 成祖晚年數北征，令山東長吏督民轉餉，道遠多死亡，惟東平人無失所。

translations.literal: In the late years of Chengzu he frequently campaigned north and ordered the chief officials of Shandong to supervise the people in transporting supplies; the roads were long and many died, but only among the people of Dongping was there no one who lost his home.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengzu's later years he frequently campaigned north and ordered Shandong's chief officials to supervise the transport of supplies; the distances were great and many people died on the road, yet no one in Dongping lost his home.

sentences.zh: 奸人誣湘苛斂民財，訐于布政司。

translations.literal: Wicked men falsely accused Xiang of harshly levying the people's wealth and reported it to the provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men falsely accused Xiang of harshly levying the people's wealth and reported him to the provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 縣民千三百人走訴巡按御史暨布、按二司，力白其冤。

translations.literal: Thirteen hundred county residents ran to appeal to the touring censor and the provincial administration and surveillance commissions, forcefully declaring his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen hundred county residents rushed to appeal to the touring censor and the provincial administration and surveillance commissions, forcefully declaring his innocence.

sentences.zh: 耆老七十人復奔伏闕下，發奸人誣陷狀。

translations.literal: Seventy elders again rushed to prostrate themselves below the palace gate, exposing the wicked men's false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy elders again rushed to prostrate themselves before the palace gate and expose the wicked men's false accusations.

sentences.zh: 及布政司系湘入都，又有耆老九十人隨湘訟冤。

translations.literal: When the provincial administration commission took Xiang into the capital under guard, another ninety elders followed Xiang to plead his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial administration commission took Xiang into the capital under guard, another ninety elders followed him to plead his innocence.

sentences.zh: 通政司以聞，下刑曹閱實，乃復湘官，而抵奸人於法。

translations.literal: The Office of Transmission reported it; the case was sent down to the Ministry of Justice for verification, and Xiang's office was restored while the wicked men were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Transmission reported the matter; the case was sent to the Ministry of Justice for verification, Xiang's office was restored, and the wicked men were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 蒞州十餘年，至正統初，詔大臣舉郡守，尚書胡蒞以湘應，遂擢懷慶知府。

translations.literal: After more than ten years as magistrate, at the beginning of Zhengtong an edict ordered grand ministers to recommend prefects; Minister Hu Li recommended Xiang, and he was promoted to prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years as magistrate, at the beginning of the Zhengtong reign an edict ordered grand ministers to recommend prefects; Minister Hu Li recommended Xiang, and he was promoted to prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 東平民扶攜老幼，泣送數十里。

translations.literal: The people of Dongping, supporting the old and young, escorted him weeping for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Dongping, supporting the old and young, escorted him weeping for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 懷慶有軍衛，素挾勢厲民。

translations.literal: Huaizhou had military guards that habitually relied on their power to oppress the people.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhou had military guards that habitually relied on their power to oppress the people.

sentences.zh: 湘隨時裁制，皆不敢犯。

translations.literal: Xiang restrained them as occasions arose, and none dared transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang restrained them as the need arose, and none dared transgress.

sentences.zh: 居三年卒。

translations.literal: After three years in office he died.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he died.

sentences.zh: 趙豫，字定素，安肅人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu, styled Dingsu, was a man of Ansu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu, styled Dingsu, was a native of Ansu.

sentences.zh: 燕王起兵下保定，豫以諸生督賦守城。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yan raised troops and took Baoding, Yu as a common scholar supervised tax collection and defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan raised troops and captured Baoding, Yu, then a common scholar, supervised tax collection and helped defend the city.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年授泌陽主簿，未上，擢兵部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongle he was appointed registrar of Biyang; before taking up the post he was promoted to secretary of the Ministry of War and advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongle (1407) he was appointed registrar of Biyang, but before taking up the post he was promoted to secretary of the Ministry of War and then advanced to vice director.

sentences.zh: 內艱起復。

translations.literal: After mourning for his mother he returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother he returned to office.

sentences.zh: 洪熙時進郎中。

translations.literal: During Hongxi he was promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongxi reign he was promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年五月簡廷臣九人為知府，豫得松江，奉敕往。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Xuande, nine court officials were selected as prefects; Yu received Songjiang and departed under imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Xuande (1430), nine court officials were selected as prefects; Yu was assigned to Songjiang and sent out under imperial command.

sentences.zh: 時衛軍恣橫，豫執其尤者，杖而配之邊，眾遂貼然。

translations.literal: At the time garrison soldiers were arrogant and violent; Yu seized the worst offenders, beat them and banished them to the frontier, and the rest promptly subsided.
translations.idiomatic: At the time garrison soldiers were arrogant and violent; Yu seized the worst offenders, had them beaten and banished to the frontier, and the rest promptly fell into line.

sentences.zh: 一意拊循，與民休息。

translations.literal: He devoted himself entirely to comforting and guiding the people, letting them rest.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself entirely to comforting and guiding the people and giving them respite.

sentences.zh: 擇良家子謹厚者為吏，訓以禮法。

translations.literal: He chose sons of good families who were prudent and sincere to serve as clerks, and instructed them in ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: He chose prudent and sincere sons of good families to serve as clerks and instructed them in ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 均徭節費，減吏員十之五。

translations.literal: He equalized corvée and cut expenses, reducing clerical staff by five-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: He equalized corvée obligations and cut expenses, reducing clerical staff by half.

sentences.zh: 巡撫周忱有所建置，必與豫議。

translations.literal: Whenever Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen had plans to establish something, he always consulted Yu first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen planned some new measure, he always consulted Yu first.

sentences.zh: 及清軍御史李立至，專務益軍，勾及姻戚同姓。

translations.literal: When army-clearing censor Li Li arrived, he devoted himself solely to augmenting the army and implicated even affinal kin and those sharing a surname.
translations.idiomatic: When army-clearing censor Li Li arrived, he devoted himself solely to augmenting the army and implicated even affinal relatives and people who merely shared a surname.

sentences.zh: 稍辨，則酷刑榜掠。

translations.literal: The slightest protest brought cruel torture and beating.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest protest brought cruel torture and beating.

sentences.zh: 人情大擾，訴枉者至一千一百餘人。

translations.literal: Public sentiment was greatly disturbed; those appealing injustice reached more than eleven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Public sentiment was greatly disturbed, and more than eleven hundred people appealed that they had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 鹽司勾灶丁，亦累及他戶，大為民害。

translations.literal: The salt commission's conscription of saltern workers also dragged in other households—a great harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The salt commission's conscription of saltern workers also dragged in other households, greatly harming the people.

sentences.zh: 豫皆上章極論之，咸獲蘇息。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized forcefully on all these matters, and all obtained relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized forcefully on all these matters, and in each case the people obtained relief.

sentences.zh: 有詔滅蘇、松官田重租，豫所轄華亭、上海二縣，減去十之二三。

translations.literal: An edict reduced the heavy rents on official fields in Suzhou and Songjiang; in Huating and Shanghai, the two counties under Yu's jurisdiction, rents were cut by two or three tenths.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict reduced the heavy rents on official fields in Suzhou and Songjiang, rents in Huating and Shanghai, the two counties under Yu's jurisdiction, were cut by twenty or thirty percent.

sentences.zh: 正統中，九載考績。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong, at the nine-year performance review.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, at the nine-year performance review.

sentences.zh: 民五千餘人列狀乞留，巡按御史以聞，命增二秩還任。

translations.literal: More than five thousand people filed petitions asking him to stay; the touring censor reported it, and he was ordered promoted two ranks and returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: More than five thousand people filed petitions asking that he be kept in office; the touring censor reported this, and he was ordered promoted two ranks and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 及十年春，大計群吏，始舉卓異之典。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year, at the great evaluation of officials, the ceremony for marking exceptional merit was held for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year, at the great evaluation of officials, the ceremony for marking exceptional merit was held for the first time.

sentences.zh: 豫與甯國知府袁旭皆預焉，賜宴及襲衣遣還。

translations.literal: Yu and Yuan Xu, prefect of Ningguo, both participated; they were granted a banquet and ceremonial robes and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Yuan Xu, prefect of Ningguo, both took part; they were granted a banquet and ceremonial robes and sent back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 在職十五年，清靜如一日。

translations.literal: Throughout fifteen years in office he remained as pure and tranquil as on the first day.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout fifteen years in office he remained as pure and tranquil as on the first day.

sentences.zh: 去郡，老稚攀轅，留一履以識遺愛，後配享周忱祠。

translations.literal: When he left the prefecture, old and young clung to his carriage shafts; they kept one of his sandals as a token of his enduring affection, and he was later accorded secondary worship in Zhou Chen's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the prefecture, old and young clung to his carriage shafts; they kept one of his sandals as a token of his enduring affection, and he was later accorded secondary worship in Zhou Chen's shrine.

sentences.zh: 方豫始至，患民俗多訟。

translations.literal: When Yu first arrived, he was troubled that local custom involved much litigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu first arrived, he was troubled by the local custom of frequent litigation.

sentences.zh: 訟者至，輒好言諭之曰：「明日來。」

translations.literal: When litigants came, he would gently persuade them, saying: "Come back tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: When litigants came, he would gently persuade them, saying: "Come back tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 眾皆笑之，有「松江太守明日來」之謠。

translations.literal: All laughed at this, and there was a ballad: "The Songjiang prefect will come tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone laughed at this, and a ballad circulated: "The Songjiang prefect will come tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 及訟者逾宿忿漸平，或被勸阻，多止不訟。

translations.literal: When litigants passed a night, their anger gradually subsided, or they were dissuaded by others, and most ceased their lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: After a night's sleep, litigants' anger usually subsided, or others talked them out of proceeding, and most dropped their suits.

sentences.zh: 始與豫同守郡者，蘇州況鐘、常州莫愚、吉水陳本深、溫州何文淵、杭州馬儀、西安羅以禮、建昌陳鼎，並皦皦著名績，豫尤以愷悌稱。

translations.literal: Those who had originally served as prefects together with Yu included Kuang Zhong of Suzhou, Mo Yu of Changzhou, Chen Benshen of Jishui, He Wenyuan of Wenzhou, Ma Yi of Hangzhou, Luo Yili of Xi'an, and Chen Ding of Jianchang—all bright and famous in achievement; Yu was especially praised for kindness and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had originally served as prefects alongside Yu included Kuang Zhong of Suzhou, Mo Yu of Changzhou, Chen Benshen of Jishui, He Wenyuan of Wenzhou, Ma Yi of Hangzhou, Luo Yili of Xi'an, and Chen Ding of Jianchang—all renowned for their bright and distinguished achievements. Yu was especially praised for his kind and easy manner.

sentences.zh: 是時，列郡長吏以惠政著聞者：

translations.literal: At this time, among the chief officials of the various prefectures who were famed for benevolent governance:
translations.idiomatic: At this time, among the chief officials of the various prefectures who were famed for benevolent governance:

sentences.zh: 湖州知府祥符趙登，秩滿當遷。

translations.literal: Zhao Deng of Xiangfu, prefect of Huzhou, reached the end of his term and was due for transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Deng of Xiangfu, prefect of Huzhou, reached the end of his term and was due for transfer.

sentences.zh: 民詣闕乞留，增秩再任，自宣德至正統，先後在官十七年。

translations.literal: The people went to the capital to petition that he be kept in office; his rank was raised and he was reappointed; from Xuande through Zhengtong he served in office seventeen years altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The people went to the capital to petition that he be kept in office; his rank was raised and he was reappointed. From Xuande through Zhengtong he served altogether seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 登同里嶽璿繼之，亦有善政，民稱為趙、嶽。

translations.literal: Yue Xuan of the same native place succeeded him and also had good governance; the people called them Zhao and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Xuan of the same native place succeeded him and also governed well; the people referred to them as "Zhao and Yue."

sentences.zh: 淮安知府南昌彭遠被誣當罷，民擁中官舟，乞為奏請，宣帝命復留之。

translations.literal: Peng Yuan of Nanchang, prefect of Huai'an, was falsely accused and due to be dismissed; the people blocked an eunuch's boat and begged that a memorial be submitted on his behalf; the Xuande Emperor ordered that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuan of Nanchang, prefect of Huai'an, was falsely accused and due to be dismissed; the people blocked an eunuch's boat and begged that a memorial be submitted on his behalf. The Xuande Emperor ordered that he be retained.

sentences.zh: 正統六年超擢廣東布政司。
